Utilizing Critical Point Theory, we establish the existence of non-trivial solutions subject to the Ambrosetti-Rabinowitz condition and demonstrate the existence of ground-state solutions. Additionally, we present multiplicity results indicating an unbounded sequence of solutions. Furthermore, we prove existence under a weak-type Ambrosetti-Rabinowitz condition adapted to the Orlicz space framework.

This study examines the discrete Allen-Cahn equation featuring cubic and quintic nonlinearities on a Lieb lattice, focusing on localized nonlinear solutions characterized by linear multistability and hysteresis within their bifurcation diagrams. We specifically analyze the system's homoclinic snaking—a snaking-like pattern in the bifurcation diagram—with an emphasis on how lattice structure influences this phenomenon. To derive localized solutions along the bifurcation diagram, we employ numerical continuation via a pseudoarclength method. Furthermore, we introduce an active-cell approximation to categorize solution types at turning points, demonstrating strong agreement with numerical data under conditions of weak coupling. Finally, the time dynamics of localized solutions both within and outside the pinning region are explored.

We generalize the Feynman variational approach \cite{Feynman1955}, originally developed for the polaron problem, to address the Holstein (lattice) polaron. This novel framework reveals a discrete transition to the small-polaron regime within the Holstein model. Furthermore, the method is directly applicable to the FHIP \cite{Feynman1962} mobility theory for computing dc mobility and complex impedance. By incorporating matrix elements derived from electronic structure calculations on actual materials, we successfully modeled charge-carrier mobility in crystalline rubrene. Our results demonstrate strong agreement with experimental data, particularly regarding the continuous thermal shift in mobility from band-like to thermally activated behavior, which includes a predicted mobility minimum at 140 K.

We identify two characteristics of axion cosmology with potential cosmological significance, regardless of whether axions constitute dark matter. Across the entire spectrum of permissible axion masses, the evolution of a cosmic axion background sustains significant CP violation down to temperatures around $\sim$ 2 GeV. Furthermore, when the axion field initiates oscillation, its relaxation toward the ground state can momentarily induce a departure from thermal equilibrium through time-dependent CP violation. In both scenarios, the Strong CP violating parameter $\bar\theta$ can reach magnitudes of order O(1).

Language models (LMs) are employed in both engineering and cognitive research to calculate information-theoretic complexity metrics that mimic human cognitive load during reading. However, this study identifies a key limitation of using modern neural LMs for this purpose: a mismatch exists between their context access capabilities and those of humans. Our findings indicate that restricting LMs' context access enhances their ability to simulate human reading behavior. Furthermore, we observed that discrepancies in context access between LMs and humans correspond to particular syntactic structures; integrating syntactic biases into how LMs access context could improve their cognitive plausibility.

Hadronic light-by-light scattering represents a key virtual mechanism responsible for the deviation of the muon's gyromagnetic factor, $g$, from the value of two predicted by Dirac's theory. This process constitutes a major source of uncertainty in the Standard Model's prediction for the muon $(g-2)$. Lattice Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) offers a first-principles method to calculate this non-perturbative phenomenon. To circumvent power-law finite-size artifacts arising from virtual photons in lattice simulations, we adopt a coordinate-space strategy that utilizes a weighted integral over the vertices of the quark electromagnetic current's QCD four-point function. In this work, we detail the semi-analytical computation of the QED component of the amplitude, utilizing position-space perturbation theory within continuous, infinite four-dimensional Euclidean space. Additionally, we provide practical details regarding a publicly available computer code for the numerical execution of our method, hosted at https://github.com/RJHudspith/KQED.

The Gaia mission's third data release (DR3) marks a significant milestone as the first to deliver a substantial dataset for over 150,000 Solar System objects, encompassing asteroids and natural satellites. This release includes astrometric data spanning more than 23 million epochs, photometric information, osculating orbital elements, and mean reflectance spectra for 60,518 asteroids. We provide an overview of the multi-year development and testing procedures required to process Solar System data with Gaia's high precision, illustrating the dataset's characteristics and potential through practical examples. To assist users in maximizing the utility of DR3, we detail the assumptions and methodologies underpinning the data processing pipeline, specifically regarding data filtering, optimization, and performance outcomes. Furthermore, we evaluate data quality by examining post-fit residuals from adjusted orbits, assessing the ability to detect subtle dynamical phenomena such as satellite-induced or shape-related wobbling and the Yarkovsky acceleration, and verifying the reproduction of known asteroid photometric properties like phase and rotational light curves. The astrometric precision in DR3 represents a marked improvement over the limited asteroid sample in DR2. The effectiveness of the data reduction is demonstrated by the detection of milliarcsecond-level photocentre wobbles caused by satellites or shape effects, which are crucial for measuring the Yarkovsky effect. Ultimately, in terms of both completeness and accuracy, DR3 constitutes the first full-scale realization of Gaia's Solar System survey.

The principle of least action stands as one of the most fundamental concepts in physics, positing that among all possible motions between two points in phase space, a system follows paths that extremize an action functional. Many qualitative aspects of dynamical systems, including conservation laws and energy balance equations, stem from the existence of such a functional. Consequently, embedding variational structures into learning algorithms for dynamical systems is essential to ensure that the resulting models retain key characteristics of the exact physical system. This paper demonstrates how to integrate variational principles into trajectory predictions for learned dynamical systems. The novelty of our approach lies in three areas: (1) our method relies exclusively on discrete position data from observed trajectories, requiring no observation or approximation of velocities or conjugate momenta, nor any prior knowledge of the variational principle's form; instead, these quantities are recovered via backward error analysis. (2) Furthermore, our technique compensates for discretization errors during trajectory computation from the learned system, a critical feature when moderate to large step-sizes are employed to achieve high accuracy. To this end, we introduce and rigorously analyze the concept of inverse modified Lagrangians by developing an inverse variant of variational backward error analysis. (3) Finally, we present a method for system identification based solely on position observations, grounded in variational backward error analysis.

This short survey serves as an introduction to and summary of key concepts discussed at the 2017 American Institute of Mathematics Workshop on Singular Geometry and Higgs Bundles in String Theory (October 30th–November 3rd). A central highlight of the string theory duality revolution is the realization that gauge fields and matter representations arise from the intersection of branes. Given that gauge theory fundamentally underpins our description of physical interactions, this insight has facilitated the geometric engineering of numerous physical systems, especially those involving Higgs bundles. The following note offers a curated selection of recent advancements and unresolved questions within this field, explicitly not intended as a comprehensive review.

The Sinkhorn operator has recently gained significant traction in computer vision and associated domains, largely due to its seamless integration with deep learning frameworks. To facilitate efficient training of neural networks incorporating this operator, we introduce an algorithm that computes analytical gradients for a Sinkhorn layer using implicit differentiation. Unlike previous approaches, our framework relies on the most general formulation of the Sinkhorn operator, supporting any loss function while jointly differentiating both target capacities and cost matrices. Additionally, we establish error bounds for the algorithm when applied to approximate inputs. Our results demonstrate that replacing standard automatic differentiation with our method directly enhances the stability and accuracy of gradient computations across various applications. Furthermore, we show that this approach offers superior computational efficiency, particularly in scenarios where resources such as GPU memory are limited.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be $C^{\ast}$-algebras. A linear map $\phi: \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ is termed a $C^{\ast}$-Jordan homomorphism if it acts as a Jordan homomorphism and maintains the adjoint operation. This note demonstrates that, subject to mild assumptions, such $C^{\ast}$-Jordan homomorphisms preserve both the covariance set and the covariance coset within $C^{\ast}$-algebras.

We examine the junction formed by a Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer superconductor and a non-superconducting band insulator. Our findings indicate that under specific conditions, these interfaces can exhibit an enhanced superconducting critical temperature without requiring a stronger pairing interaction at the boundary. Furthermore, we determine the parameter regimes in which the critical temperature of such an interface surpasses that of a superconductor-vacuum interface.

In 1989, Carsten Thomassen conjectured that any graph with a minimum degree exceeding the number of atoms in the universe ($\delta(G)\ge 10^{10^{10}}$) must contain a "pillar." A pillar is defined as a structure comprising two vertex-disjoint cycles of identical length, $s$, connected by $s$ vertex-disjoint paths of the same length, linking matching vertices sequentially around the cycles. Despite the structural simplicity of pillars and significant advancements in embedding methods for paths and cycles over the last thirty years, this seemingly straightforward conjecture has remained unproven until now. This paper presents a proof of the conjecture by demonstrating an algorithmic construction of pillars within sublinear expanders.

This study employs molecular dynamics simulations to examine how tensile stress applied during the cooling of binary glasses influences potential energy states and mechanical properties. The research focuses on a three-dimensional binary mixture that undergoes annealing near the glass transition temperature before being rapidly cooled under tension into the glass phase. Results indicate that at higher stress levels, the liquid precursor solidifies at greater strains with elevated potential energy. Additionally, for a constant cooling rate, the maximum sustainable tensile stress decreases as the initial temperature rises above the glass transition point. The amorphous structure of these rejuvenated glasses is marked by an increased number of contacts among smaller atoms. Furthermore, tensile testing reveals that both the elastic modulus and the peak stress overshoot are diminished in glasses formed under larger stresses and higher initial temperatures, suggesting improved ductility. These insights could aid in developing processing techniques to enhance the plasticity of bulk metallic glasses.

Recent research has detailed the synthesis and analysis of various bulk crystals of layered metal triselenophosphites, MPSe$_3$ (where M represents transition metals). These studies employed a suite of both bulk- and surface-sensitive experimental techniques alongside DFT calculations. However, a rigorous review of the existing experimental and theoretical evidence indicates that the findings do not substantiate claims regarding the material's potential for electrochemical sensing and energy applications. Such conclusions appear to be drawn without accounting for the age of the data or advancements in both experimental and theoretical methodologies.

We derive an observation inequality for the Schrödinger equation on $\mathbf{R}^d$ that remains uniform with respect to the Planck constant $\hbar\in[0,1]$. This proof relies on the pseudometric presented in [F. Golse, T. Paul, Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 223 (2017), 57-94]. The resulting inequality features solely effective constants, with their explicit dependence on $\hbar$ and all relevant parameters calculated directly.

This study introduces an efficient exponential integrator finite element method designed for solving semilinear parabolic equations within rectangular domains. The approach begins by applying spatial discretization via the finite element method, utilizing continuous multilinear rectangular basis functions, followed by explicit exponential Runge-Kutta integration for the resulting semi-discrete system to generate fully discrete numerical solutions. Assuming specific regularity conditions, we derive error estimates in the $H^1$-norm for schemes employing one and two Runge-Kutta stages. Notably, the method allows for the simultaneous diagonalization of both mass and coefficient matrices using an orthogonal matrix, enabling rapid computation through tensor product spectral decomposition and fast Fourier transforms. Additionally, extensive numerical experiments in two and three dimensions are conducted to confirm the theoretical findings and highlight the method's superior performance.

Lasso is a popular regression method designed to identify sparse solutions. However, when both the feature dimension and sample size are massive, solving the Lasso problem becomes difficult. To enhance efficiency in large-scale Lasso scenarios, El Ghaoui and colleagues introduced the SAFE rules, which rapidly detect inactive predictors—those with zero coefficients in the solution. These inactive features can then be eliminated from the optimization to reduce its scale. By converting the standard Lasso into its dual form, it is demonstrated that inactive predictors correspond to inactive constraints in the optimal dual solution. This paper presents an efficient and effective screening rule based on Dual Polytope Projections (DPP). This approach leverages the uniqueness and nonexpansiveness of the optimal dual solution, relying on the fact that the feasible region in the dual space is a convex, closed polytope. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this screening rule can be extended to identify inactive groups within the group Lasso framework; to our knowledge, no exact screening rule for group Lasso currently exists. Evaluations on both synthetic and real datasets indicate that our rule outperforms existing state-of-the-art screening methods in identifying inactive predictors for Lasso.

The core challenge in text-to-image synthesis lies in maintaining semantic consistency across modalities between the input text and the resulting image. Conventional approaches that model this mapping directly often only recognize keywords denoting common objects or actions, neglecting their spatial arrangement. A viable solution to this issue is generating an image layout as a guide, a strategy attempted by several existing methods. However, these approaches struggle to produce practically useful layouts due to the variability in input text and object positioning. This paper addresses effective modeling for both text-to-layout generation and layout-to-image synthesis. We frame text-to-layout generation as a sequence-to-sequence task, utilizing a Transformer architecture to capture spatial relationships by modeling sequential dependencies among objects. During the layout-to-image synthesis phase, we emphasize learning textual-visual semantic alignment for each object within the layout to accurately integrate the input text into the synthesis process. To assess layout quality, we introduce a novel metric called the Layout Quality Score, which accounts for both absolute bounding box distribution errors and the mutual spatial relationships between them. Extensive experiments across three datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in both layout prediction and text-to-image synthesis.

Entropy-based approaches have garnered significant critical attention for quantifying system complexity in real-world data analysis. However, amplitude-based algorithms, such as Sample Entropy, face limitations regarding data length, a drawback that becomes more pronounced when coarse graining is applied in multi-scale processes. This imbalance between embedding dimension and available data size inevitably leads to inaccurate or undefined estimations. To address this issue, this paper proposes the Variational Embedding Multiscale Sample Entropy, which assigns distinct embedding dimensions to signals from different channels. The algorithm was evaluated using both simulated and real signals. Its performance was further investigated through comparisons with Multivariate Multiscale Sample Entropy and Variational Embedding Multiscale Diversity Entropy, utilizing two real-world databases: wind datasets with varying regimes and physiological data recorded from young and elderly individuals. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves improved separation in both scenarios.

Symmetric Teleparallel Gravity stands out as a unique gravitational theory compatible with a vanishing affine connection. It offers a more streamlined geometrical alternative to general relativity, wherein gravitational interaction is governed by non-metricity ($Q$). This study investigates cosmological bouncing scenarios within a flat Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) spacetime under this framework. Specifically, we analyze bouncing models utilizing two distinct $f(Q)$ Lagrangian forms: one with linear dependence on $Q$ and another with non-linear dependence. For both cases, we have thoroughly verified all energy conditions and conducted stability analyses to demonstrate a viable matter bounce.

Determining causal relationships between event types within multi-type event sequences is a critical yet difficult endeavor. Current approaches, including Multivariate Hawkes processes, largely rely on the assumption that sequences are independent and identically distributed. However, real-world scenarios frequently involve an underlying topological network where an event's excitation or inhibition is influenced not only by its own history but also by its neighbors in the network. This omission of topological dependencies in existing models often results in inaccurate causal structure detection. By viewing Hawkes processes through the lens of temporal convolution, we introduce the Topological Hawkes process (THP), which bridges graph convolution in the topological domain with temporal convolution in the time domain. We also present a likelihood-based method for learning causal structures within the THP framework. This approach is characterized by a graph convolution-derived likelihood function and a sparse optimization strategy utilizing an Expectation-Maximization algorithm to maximize that likelihood. Both theoretical analysis and experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets confirm the efficacy of our proposed method.

This study investigates whether spatially flat $\Lambda$CDM-like evolution in FLRW cosmologies within General Relativity is unique, specifically examining if alternative models can replicate the same scale factor dynamics. We clarify the difference between \emph{kinematic} and \emph{dynamic} equivalence. Focusing on two interacting dark sector models—the coupled fluid-fluid model and the coupled quintessence model—we impose a \emph{kinematic} degeneracy with spatially flat $\Lambda$CDM by enforcing the cosmographic condition $j=1$ (where $j$ denotes the jerk parameter), thereby determining the previously unspecified interaction function. We demonstrate that within General Relativity, this condition is compatible only with spatial flatness. Using a dynamical systems approach, we find that spatially flat coupled fluid-fluid models kinematically degenerate with $\Lambda$CDM must rely on phantom fluids, while physically viable spatially flat coupled quintessence models with power-law or exponential potentials that achieve such degeneracy constitute a set of measure zero. Consequently, coupled fluid-fluid models involving non-phantom fluids or coupled quintessence models with power-law and exponential potentials cannot mimic $\Lambda$CDM evolution. Finally, we discuss the astrophysical implications of these results in the context of current observational cosmological tensions.

Following the discovery of a particle matching the Higgs boson's properties predicted by the Standard Model, particle physics has entered a thrilling new phase. A key inquiry remains whether Nature's scalar sector aligns with Standard Model predictions or if the 125 GeV resonance signals a broader scalar sector, potentially allowing for the observation of extra scalar states at existing or upcoming collider facilities.

A C-metric solution for general relativity with a cosmological constant is introduced in 2+1 dimensions, representing a three-dimensional black hole accelerated by a strut. The analysis also accommodates positive cosmological constant values. Furthermore, various embeddings of this metric into 3+1 space-time are examined, including an accelerating BTZ black string and a black ring where gravity is maintained by acceleration.

The discrepancy between the masses of charged and neutral pions arises from both QCD and QED effects, with the QCD component stemming from the difference in current quark masses ($\Delta m$). Within a two-flavor non-local NJL framework, we aim to estimate this QCD contribution. Our findings indicate that the parameter $c$, which governs $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking, is essential for reproducing the pion mass difference, acting in conjunction with $\Delta m$. By scanning the parameter space defined by $\{\Delta m, c\}$ and comparing our results with established data, we can constrain these parameters. Additionally, utilizing a fitted value for $c$ allows us to establish the permissible range for the current quark mass difference within the model.

This study presents measurements of the joint polarization states of $W$ and $Z$ gauge bosons produced in $W^{\pm}Z$ events. The analysis utilizes a dataset of $139$ fb$^{-1}$ of proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of $13$ TeV, recorded by the ATLAS detector at the CERN Large Hadron Collider. Candidate $W^{\pm}Z$ events are identified through the leptonic decays of these bosons into electrons and muons. For the first time, the simultaneous production of longitudinally polarized vector bosons is observed with a statistical significance of $7.1$ standard deviations. The measured joint helicity fractions, integrated over the fiducial region, are $f_{\mathrm{00}} = 0.067 \pm 0.010$, $f_{\mathrm{0T}} = 0.110 \pm 0.029$, $f_{\mathrm{T0}} = 0.179 \pm 0.023$, and $f_{\mathrm{TT}} = 0.644 \pm 0.032$, which align with next-to-leading-order Standard Model predictions. Additionally, the individual helicity fractions for the $W$ and $Z$ bosons are determined and found to be consistent with the joint fractions within expected correlation limits. These measurements are performed separately for $W^+Z$ and $W^-Z$ events. Furthermore, inclusive and differential cross sections for various kinematic variables sensitive to polarization are reported.

Sagittarius A*, the black hole at the Galactic Center, relies on the blazar J1924-2914 as a key calibrator for the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT). This study introduces the first total and linearly polarized intensity images of J1924-2914, captured with the EHT's unprecedented 20 microarcsecond resolution. J1924-2914 is a highly compact, flat-spectrum radio source known for significant optical variability and polarization. In April 2017, the source was observed quasi-simultaneously by the EHT (April 5–11), the Global Millimeter VLBI Array (April 3), and the Very Long Baseline Array (April 28), providing a unique multi-frequency perspective at 230, 86, 8.7, and 2.3 GHz. These observations investigate jet characteristics across scales ranging from subparsec to 100 parsecs. By combining multi-frequency images, we analyze the source's morphology and identify a distinct jet bend, marked by a gradual clockwise rotation of approximately 90 degrees in the projected position angle between 2.3 and 230 GHz. Furthermore, the extremely high-resolution linearly polarized images from the EHT offer evidence of ordered toroidal magnetic fields within the blazar's compact core.

The Kakeya conjecture is typically expressed in one of two ways: either that any compact, Borel, or arbitrary subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ containing a unit line segment in every direction must have a Hausdorff dimension of $n$, or that any closed, Borel, or arbitrary subset containing a full line in every direction must have a Hausdorff dimension of $n$. These formulations are generally believed to be equivalent. Furthermore, the requirement that a set contains lines or segments in all directions is frequently relaxed to apply only to a "large" collection of directions, defined as having positive $(n-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. This work establishes the equivalence of all aforementioned forms of the conjecture. Specifically, we demonstrate the existence of a compact set $C$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with Hausdorff dimension $d \le n$ that includes a unit line segment in every direction (and a closed set of dimension $d$ containing a line in every direction), such that any subset $S$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ containing line segments in all directions of a set with Hausdorff dimension $n-1$ must possess a dimension of at least $d$. Additionally, we present findings regarding the duality between Hausdorff and packing dimensions through additive complements: for any non-empty Borel set $A$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, (1) the Hausdorff dimension of $A$ equals $n-p$, where $p$ is the infimum of the packing dimensions of Borel sets $B$ such that $A+B=\mathbb{R}^n$, and (2) the packing dimension of $A$ equals $n-h$, where $h$ is the infimum of the Hausdorff dimensions of Borel sets $B$ such that $A+B=\mathbb{R}^n$.

Variance reduction (VR) techniques for finite-sum minimization generally depend on problem-specific constants that are frequently unknown and hard to estimate. To overcome this limitation, we adapt concepts from adaptive gradient methods to introduce AdaSVRG, a more resilient version of the widely used SVRG algorithm. By integrating AdaGrad into SVRG's inner loop, AdaSVRG becomes less sensitive to step-size selection. We demonstrate that when minimizing a sum of $n$ smooth convex functions, a variant of AdaSVRG achieves $O(\epsilon)$-suboptimality with $\tilde{O}(n + 1/\epsilon)$ gradient evaluations, matching standard rates without requiring prior knowledge of problem-dependent constants. Furthermore, we exploit AdaGrad's characteristics to devise a heuristic that adaptively sets the inner-loop length. Experiments on both synthetic and real-world data confirm the method's robustness and efficacy, showing it outperforms standard and other "tune-free" VR approaches.

Genetic algorithms possess distinctive characteristics that make them particularly effective for black-box optimization tasks. By utilizing selection, crossover, and mutation operators, these algorithms can generate candidate solutions without requiring gradient calculations. This study investigates the integration of quantum-enhanced operators into the selection phase of genetic algorithms. Our methodology models the selection process as minimizing a binary quadratic representation of fitness and population distance, employing a quantum annealing system to sample low-energy solutions for this mechanism. We evaluated these quantum-enhanced algorithms against classical counterparts across diverse black-box objective functions, including the OneMax function and benchmarks from the IOHProfiler library. Our results indicate an improvement in the average number of generations required for convergence when using quantum-enhanced elitist selection on the OneMax function. Furthermore, quantum-enhanced non-elitist selection outperformed benchmarks on IOHProfiler functions involving fitness perturbation. Finally, in scenarios with elitist selection, quantum-enhanced operators demonstrated superiority over classical benchmarks on functions characterized by varying levels of dummy variables and neutrality.

To comprehend the cosmic accretion history of supermassive black holes, it is essential to distinguish between radiation from active galactic nuclei (AGNs) and star-forming galaxies (SFGs); however, a robust photometric method for identifying AGNs remains elusive. This study introduces a novel AGN recognition approach utilizing a Deep Neural Network (NN). Our primary objectives are: (i) to evaluate whether an NN can resolve the AGN recognition challenge within the North Ecliptic Pole Wide (NEPW) field; (ii) to demonstrate that the NN outperforms traditional spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting techniques in our test samples; and (iii) to publicly distribute a reliable AGN/SFG catalogue based on the highest-quality available NEPW data, alongside proposing an enhanced methodology to guide future NEPW database development. Experimental results indicate that the NN achieves a recognition accuracy between 80.29% and 85.15%, with AGN completeness ranging from 85.42% to 88.53% and SFG completeness between 81.17% and 85.09%.

We demonstrate that for an RSII braneworld containing interacting viscous dark energy and dark matter, the Friedmann equation can consistently be reformulated as the first law of thermodynamics, $dE=T_hdS_h+WdV$, at the apparent horizon. Furthermore, the generalized second law of thermodynamics holds within the region bounded by the apparent horizon on the brane, applicable to both constant and time-varying 5-dimensional Newton's constant $G_5$. These findings remain valid irrespective of the specific dark energy equation of state. Our research further corroborates that in an accelerating universe with spatial curvature, the apparent horizon functions as a physical boundary from a thermodynamic perspective.

To better understand the limitations of class-level documentation, we surveyed 167 experienced software developers. The survey focused on the participants' programming-related information needs and how frequently class-level documentation meets those needs.

This paper provides a comprehensive characterization of all indecomposable characters (central positive-definite functions) associated with inductive limits of symmetric groups formed via block diagonal embedding. As a consequence, we derive a complete classification of the isomorphism classes of these inductive limits.

Skin cancer ranks among the top three most prevalent cancers globally, with melanoma being especially hazardous due to its metastatic potential. While early detection is crucial for successful treatment, diagnosing skin cancer remains difficult even for seasoned dermatologists because benign and malignant lesions often appear very similar. To assist medical professionals, we created a deep learning system capable of automatically categorizing skin lesions into seven distinct categories: Actinic Keratoses, Basal Cell Carcinoma, Benign Keratosis, Dermatofibroma, Melanocytic nevi, Melanoma, and Vascular Skin Lesion. The system was trained using the HAM10000 dataset and employs an end-to-end deep learning approach that leverages transfer learning with multiple pre-trained models, enhanced by class-weighted and focal loss functions. Our ensemble of modified ResNet50 models achieved top-1, top-2, and top-3 accuracies of 93%, 97%, and 99%, respectively. This technology holds the potential to be integrated into computer-aided diagnosis tools to support dermatologists in identifying skin cancer.

Android applications undergo frequent updates, typically every few weeks, to adapt to evolving user needs, hardware constraints, and business requirements. Ensuring the correctness of these updates relies heavily on rigorous testing. Although recent studies have introduced tools for automated GUI event generation in Android apps, these methods lack efficiency in validating updates because they do not prioritize modified areas but rather explore other application behaviors. This paper introduces CAT (Change-focused Android GUI Testing) to address this gap. For app updates at either the source code or GUI level, CAT conducts change impact analysis to pinpoint affected GUI elements and subsequently generates length-3 GUI event sequences specifically targeting these elements. Empirical evaluations using 21 publicly available open-source Android applications demonstrate that CAT can automatically identify update-affected GUI components and execute focused event sequences. Comparative analysis against two established tools, DroidBot and DroidMate, indicates that CAT is more effective at interacting with the modified GUI elements. Furthermore, CAT successfully detected previously unknown bugs related to changes in two of the tested applications.

Power counting serves as a systematic approach to organizing collider observables and their corresponding theoretical computations. This paper employs power counting to define a category of jet substructure observables known as energy flow polynomials (EFPs). Although EFPs form an overcomplete linear basis for infrared-and-collinear safe jet observables, practical applications often require only a limited subset for specific analyses. By utilizing power counting arguments, we derive linear relations among EFPs that are valid for quark and gluon jets up to a defined order. Validation using the parton shower generator Pythia confirms excellent agreement with these relations. Consequently, power counting enables the truncation of the EFP basis without compromising performance, a finding supported by studies on quark-gluon tagging and regression.

Managing heat flow at the nanoscale is essential for applications like thermal energy harvesting and heat management. However, designing nanostructures is difficult because phonon-boundary interactions, which Fourier's law does not account for, must be considered. While nondiffusive models such as the Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) effectively capture size effects in complex systems, their adoption has been restricted by a scarcity of open-source solvers. We address this gap with OpenBTE, an efficient solver for steady-state phonon BTE in multidimensional structures. By integrating with first-principles calculations, OpenBTE enables the computation of thermal properties without requiring fitting parameters. As a demonstration, we used OpenBTE to generate temperature and flux maps, along with mode-resolved, effective thermal conductivity for silicon membranes of both finite and infinite thickness. By facilitating rapid simulations of nanoscale heat transport, OpenBTE can accelerate the development of nanomaterials for thermal energy applications.

We demonstrate that for a boundaryless surface, no Hausdorff group topology strictly coarser than the compact-open topology exists. When combined with established automatic continuity theorems, this finding establishes that the compact-open topology is the sole Hausdorff separable group topology on the surface group, provided the surface is either closed or formed by removing from a closed surface either a finite set or the union of a finite set and a Cantor set.

Recent research has extensively investigated the exotic properties of topological Weyl semimetals (WSMs) under electric ($\vec{E}$) and magnetic ($\vec{B}$) fields. In this study, we predict the emergence of an intrinsic planar Hall effect (IPHE) in time-reversal-broken WSMs, where the Hall current, electric field, and magnetic field all lie within the same plane. We attribute this phenomenon to the (field-induced) Berry curvature, which stems from the nontrivial band geometry of WSMs and corresponds to energy corrections up to the second order under $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$. Crucially, the IPHE conductivity tensor exhibits an anti-symmetric form, dictated by the $\vec{k}$-space Lorentz force generated by this Berry curvature, distinguishing it from the symmetric form of extrinsic counterparts reported in Phys. Rev. Lett. 119, 176804 (2017). Using a linearly tilted effective model, we elucidate how the IPHE depends on the tilt direction and the angle between $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$. Notably, our analysis of angular dependence reveals that IPHE responses persist even when $\vec{E}\cdot\vec{B}=0$, suggesting that Berry curvature plays a more fundamental role than the chiral anomaly in WSMs. Finally, we discuss potential candidate materials for detecting IPHE and propose experimental strategies to differentiate the intrinsic IPHE response of WSMs from extrinsic effects. This work introduces a novel intrinsic topological response function for identifying magnetic WSMs and provides new insights into interpreting experimental observations in these materials.

Kerr-Schild perturbations within General Relativity offer a productive method for generating new exact solutions from existing ones, thereby clarifying spacetime structures. We begin this investigation within the framework of string theory and supergravity by explicitly constructing Kerr-Schild perturbations for coset conformal field theories (CFTs) rooted in low-dimensional orthogonal groups. Our analysis reveals that these perturbations yield integrable $\sigma$-models that are invariant under scaling but not Weyl transformations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these models can be obtained through a specific limiting procedure applied to $\lambda$-deformed coset CFTs based on non-compact groups. The target space of the most fundamental $\sigma$-model corresponds to a two-dimensional scale-invariant black hole, for which we present two distinct embeddings into type-II supergravity.

By nonresonantly pumping a MoS$_2$ monolayer at $13$ K with a circularly polarized continuous-wave laser, we detect exciton energy redshifts that lift the degeneracy between B excitons of opposite spins. This energy splitting grows monotonically with laser power, reaching up to $18$ meV, but decreases as temperature rises. Theoretically, this phenomenon arises from the simultaneous effects of bandgap renormalization, which causes the redshift, and exciton-exciton Coulomb exchange interactions, which drive the spin-dependent splitting. Our findings present a straightforward approach to controlling the valley degree of freedom in MoS$_2$ monolayers and offer an accessible method for probing many-body exciton-exciton interactions in these materials.

Multiple large-scale volatility matrix inference techniques have been established using latent factor models, typically assuming that a limited number of common factors drive volatility dynamics. However, various studies have shown the existence of local factors; specifically, in the context of global stock markets, nation-specific factors often explain the volatility patterns within their respective countries. To address this, we introduce the Double Principal Orthogonal complEment Thresholding (Double-POET) method, grounded in multi-level factor models, and derive its asymptotic properties. Additionally, we highlight the limitations of standard principal orthogonal component thresholding (POET) when local factor structures are present. We further illustrate the benefits of dimensionality reduction achieved through Double-POET for estimating local covariance matrices. Finally, we evaluate the Double-POET estimator's performance in an out-of-sample portfolio allocation study utilizing international stocks from 20 financial markets.

The collection of all holomorphic Euclidean isometries that preserve the Julia set of a rational map $R$ is represented as $\Sigma R$. This article demonstrates that if a root-finding method $F$ applied to a non-monomial polynomial $p$ of degree two or higher satisfies the Scaling theorem—meaning $F_p$ is affine conjugate to $F_{\lambda p \circ T}$ for any nonzero complex $\lambda$ and affine map $T$—then $\Sigma p \subseteq \Sigma F_p$. Since Chebyshev's method meets this criterion, it follows that $\Sigma p \subseteq \Sigma C_p$. The remainder of the paper investigates the conditions under which equality holds and examines the dynamics of $C_p$. We establish that the Julia set $\mathcal{J}(C_p)$ of $C_p$ cannot be a line. Furthermore, under specific scenarios where $p$ is (a) unicritical, (b) possesses exactly two roots of identical multiplicity, (c) cubic with a non-trivial $\Sigma p$, or (d) quartic, provided the centroid of $p$ is a root and $\Sigma p$ is non-trivial, we prove that $\Sigma p = \Sigma C_p$. In all these instances, the Fatou set $\mathcal{F}(C_p)$ consists of the union of all attracting basins of $C_p$ associated with the roots of $p$, and $\mathcal{J}(C_p)$ is connected. Additionally, it is noted that $\mathcal{J}(C_p)$ exhibits local connectivity in each of these cases.

This study introduces a general framework for merging physical and data-driven techniques to forecast physicochemical properties. The method incorporates physical predictions into a prior model and integrates them with sparse experimental data via Bayesian inference. When applied to estimating infinite dilution activity coefficients, this approach yields substantial performance gains over both standalone physical and data-driven baselines, as well as standard ensemble methods found in machine learning research.

We introduce a spectral clustering algorithm designed to analyze the dependence structure within multivariate extremes. Specifically, our approach targets the asymptotic dependence of these extremes, which is defined by the angular or spectral measure in extreme value theory. Our research evaluates the theoretical performance of spectral clustering using a random $k$-nearest neighbor graph derived from an extremal sample—representing the angular components of random vectors whose radii surpass a high threshold. Notably, we establish the asymptotic distribution of extremes generated by a linear factor model and demonstrate that, under specific conditions, spectral clustering can reliably identify the clusters of extremes within this framework. Building on this, we propose a straightforward consistent estimation strategy for learning the angular measure. Furthermore, our theoretical insights are supported by numerical experiments that showcase the finite sample performance of our proposed methods.

Contemporary dependence and independence logics rely on team semantics, where formula evaluation occurs over a set of variable assignments (a team) rather than a single assignment. This approach yields expressive power comparable to existential second-order logic. In contrast, Baltag and van Benthem introduced the Logic of Functional Dependence (LFD), a local variant that, despite also utilizing team semantics, evaluates formulas individually on one assignment while using the team as a pool of potential assignments. This modal perspective aligns LFD with a fragment of first-order logic, rendering its satisfiability problem decidable when equality is excluded. This work systematically extends the concept of localizing dependence and independence logics by incorporating local versions of standard atomic properties, including dependence, independence, inclusion, exclusion, and anonymity. We investigate the model-theoretic and algorithmic properties of these localized logics, addressing open questions from Baltag and van Benthem. Specifically, we analyze decidability, demonstrating that satisfiability for LFD with equality is undecidable, derive characterisation theorems using appropriate bisimulation notions, and examine the complexity of model checking for these systems.

Vacuum birefringence (VB) is a fundamental phenomenon predicted by quantum electrodynamics (QED); however, detecting it remains difficult due to the weak signal strength. Conventional approaches face a trade-off: magnet-based methods offer long interaction lengths but limited field intensity, whereas laser-driven methods provide intense fields but over short distances. To overcome this, we propose a technique for generating and detecting VB within a plasma bubble wakefield, which integrates the benefits of both by sustaining large fields over extended interaction lengths. A polarized $\gamma$-photon beam is utilized to probe the wakefield over distances ranging from millimeters to centimeters. Plasma particle-in-cell simulations indicate that the VB signal, expressed through Stokes parameters, can reach approximately $10^{-5}$ (or $10^{-3}$ to $10^{-2}$) when using moderately intense lasers ($10^{20}$-$10^{21}~\mathrm{W/cm^2}$) with tens of MeV to GeV probe photons. Noise originating from plasma electrons is significantly reduced through specific choices of $\gamma$-photon polarization and appropriate modulation of the plasma density. Consequently, this proposed method offers a promising alternative for experimentally observing VB via laser-plasma interactions.

For e-commerce enterprises offering extensive catalogs, structuring products into logical groups is essential for delivering superior shopping experiences and establishing a credible brand identity. A key method for this organization involves identifying families of product variants—items that are largely identical but differ in minor, distinct ways, such as color or package size. This paper presents a new approach to detecting these variants by integrating constrained clustering with specialized NLP techniques, such as extracting family names from unstructured titles and recognizing similar model numbers. This hybrid method outperforms existing baselines that rely on standard classification. Furthermore, the algorithm is engineered to satisfy specific business needs, ensuring high accuracy across diverse categories like appliances, decor, tools, and building materials, while prioritizing model interpretability to ensure accessibility and clarity for all stakeholders.

This paper outlines the development of DUNE, an open-source scientific software framework, driven primarily by the need for a sustainable solution for partial differential equations. We examine the strategies DUNE employs to maintain its software sustainability.

The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) stands as the Milky Way's most massive satellite, possessing an estimated mass greater than one-tenth that of our own galaxy. As it approaches its nearest point at roughly 50 kpc and passes by at a remarkable velocity of 327 km/s, the LMC influences our Galaxy significantly, potentially displacing the Milky Way's disc from its center of mass. We present evidence that the Milky Way disc is moving relative to stellar tracers in the outer halo (within $40<r<120$ kpc) at a speed of $v_{\rm travel}=32^{+4}_{-4}$ km/s, directed toward $(\ell,b)_{\rm apex}=(56^{+9}_{-9},-34^{+10}_{-9})$ degrees, which aligns with a prior position on the LMC's path. This induced reflex motion is observable in the kinematics of outer halo stars and satellite galaxies possessing precise distances, proper motions, and radial velocities. Our findings suggest that dynamical models of the Milky Way must account for gravitational disturbances caused by the LMC's infall, and that stellar halo observations cannot be analyzed without correcting for this disc reflex motion. Future spectroscopic surveys of the stellar halo, integrated with Gaia astrometry, will enable advanced modeling of the LMC's trajectory through the Milky Way, thereby constraining the dark matter distribution in both galaxies with exceptional precision.

Recent proper motion measurements indicate that PSR J0908-4913 is a rapidly moving object situated approximately 3 kpc away. We provide evidence placing this pulsar at the periphery of a newly discovered, filled-centre supernova remnant, G270.4-1.0. The pulsar's velocity vector is directed straight away from the remnant's center. This proposed link suggests an age of roughly 12 kyr for the pulsar, which is considerably younger than its characteristic age of 110 kyr. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the pulsar's rotation axis aligns with its proper motion direction. Observed temporal variations in rotation and dispersion measures likely signal the pulsar moving behind a remnant filament.

Although neural language models have largely replaced traditional $N$-gram models due to superior performance, our findings suggest that $N$-grams still yield satisfactory results in many scenarios, effectively capturing significant linguistic knowledge at a low computational cost. Leveraging this insight, we propose training a neural model to predict the residuals between an $N$-gram model and the actual data distribution. This hybrid approach enables the neural component to concentrate on deeper linguistic understanding while offering a flexible framework for customization; one can switch the underlying $N$-gram model without retraining the neural component. Experiments across three standard tasks—language modeling, machine translation, and summarization—consistently show that our method outperforms existing standalone neural models. Furthermore, the approach facilitates effective domain adaptation by simply swapping in a domain-specific $N$-gram model, requiring no additional training. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/ghrua/NgramRes.

Extracting roads from aerial imagery has become a prominent area of study within remote sensing image analysis. This letter introduces a semantic segmentation neural network designed for road area extraction, which integrates the advantages of residual learning and U-Net architectures. The model incorporates residual units and maintains a structure akin to U-Net. The advantages of this approach are twofold: residual units simplify the training of deep networks, while the extensive skip connections enhance information propagation. This enables the creation of networks with fewer parameters that achieve superior performance. The network was evaluated on a public road dataset and benchmarked against U-Net and two other leading deep learning-based road extraction techniques. The proposed method outperformed all comparison methods, highlighting its superiority over recently developed state-of-the-art approaches.

The interactive command line, or shell, serves as a primary tool for diverse software professionals, including engineers, system administrators, and data scientists. Consequently, analyzing shell customizations offers valuable insights into recurring user tasks, the adequacy of the standard environment in supporting them, and potential avenues for productive extension or modification. To characterize the patterns and complexities of command-line customization, we analyzed over 2.2 million shell alias definitions from GitHub, tapping into the collective knowledge of command-line users. Since aliases allow users to define arbitrarily complex command substitutions, we employed inductive coding methods to identify three distinct types of aliases that facilitate various customization practices: Shortcuts (used for nicknaming commands, abbreviating subcommands, and bookmarking locations), Modifications (used for substituting commands, overriding defaults, colorizing output, and elevating privilege), and Scripts (used for data transformation and chaining subcommands). We hypothesize that recognizing common customization practices can reveal specific usability issues within command-line programs, while a deeper understanding of these practices can aid researchers and tool developers in designing superior user experiences. Beyond our analysis, we offer an extensive reproducibility package comprising a curated dataset and well-documented computational notebooks, which enable further knowledge discovery and provide a foundation for developing approaches to enhance command-line workflows.

Knowledge graphs (KGs) serve as structured databases of real-world facts that encapsulate human knowledge, enabling machines to mimic human problem-solving approaches. However, because data is often incomplete and subject to rapid updates, KGs tend to be vast and inevitably contain missing facts. Link prediction aims to fill these gaps by reasoning over existing knowledge. This field is primarily divided into two research streams: one focuses on learning low-dimensional embeddings for entities and relations to capture latent patterns, while the other prioritizes interpretability by extracting logical rules. Unfortunately, prior research has largely overlooked heterogeneous KGs, which involve entities and relations of diverse types. This paper introduces DegreEmbed, a novel model that integrates embedding-based learning with logic rule mining specifically for inferring missing links in heterogeneous KGs, with a focus on node degrees. Experimental results on real-world datasets demonstrate that DegreEmbed outperforms state-of-the-art methods, while the logical rules it generates exhibit both high quality and strong interpretability.

We utilize micromagnetic simulations to illustrate the controlled creation and destruction of (anti)skyrmions featuring adjustable chirality within magnetic heterostructures. By employing magnetic (anti)vortices in structured ferromagnetic layers, we achieve the reproducible stabilization of complete (anti)skyrmion lattices within a skyrmionic thin film. The stability of these (anti)skyrmions is governed by the polarization of the associated (anti)vortices, while their chirality is determined by the chirality of the (anti)vortices. Additionally, we show that the core coupling between (anti)vortices and (anti)skyrmions enables the controlled annihilation of these spin objects through brief in-plane magnetic field pulses, establishing a novel paradigm for skyrmionic devices.

The characteristics and origins of free-floating planets (FFPs) remain poorly understood due to the absence of large, uniform datasets required for statistical analysis. Currently, most FFPs are detected via indirect techniques, with microlensing surveys being especially effective at identifying objects as small as a few Earth masses. However, the transient nature of these events precludes follow-up observations or detailed characterization of individual objects. While previous studies have located FFPs in young stellar clusters and the Galactic field, their sample sizes are limited and often inconsistent regarding age and origin. This study reports the detection of 70 to 170 FFPs (depending on the assumed age) within the Upper Scorpius and Ophiuchus region, the nearest young OB association to the Sun. Our findings reveal an FFP excess of up to seven times the rate predicted by core-collapse models, suggesting alternative formation mechanisms are active. We estimate that ejection from planetary systems contributes as much as core-collapse to FFP formation. Consequently, dynamical instabilities in giant exoplanet systems causing ejections must occur frequently within the first 10 million years of a system's evolution.

Forests are essential to planetary health, yet widespread deforestation globally endangers climate stability, biodiversity, and fragile ecosystems. As public concern over climate change and forest conservation grows, the demand for carbon offsetting, footprint assessments, and environmental impact studies is surging. Traditionally, deforestation maps rely on optical data like Landsat and MODIS; however, frequent cloud cover, particularly in the tropics where most forest biomass exists, limits these maps to annual intervals. Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) offers a solution by penetrating clouds. This study proposes and evaluates a novel deforestation detection method that operates without reliable reference data, a common practical obstacle. The approach achieved a producer's accuracy of 96.5% in the study area, though user's accuracy dropped to approximately 75.7% due to false positives, resulting in a balanced accuracy of 90.4%. This detection accuracy remained stable even with up to 20% noise in the reference labels. Although further research is needed to minimize false positives, reduce detection latency, and validate the method across various scenarios, the findings indicate that Sentinel-1 data can significantly improve the timeliness of global deforestation monitoring.

Shortcut learning arises when deep neural networks excessively depend on spurious correlations within training data to solve tasks, a phenomenon previously shown to hinder compositional generalization. To counteract this issue in uncontrolled target domains, we introduce a novel method that mitigates shortcut learning by augmenting the training set with a specialized source domain. This source domain is curated to encourage the learning of independent representations for fundamental visual factors. We evaluate our approach on both synthetic target domains, where shortcut opportunities are explicitly controlled, and real-world scenarios. Additionally, we examine how varying specifications of the source domain and network architecture influence compositional generalization. Our primary conclusion is that utilizing data from a source domain effectively reduces shortcut learning. By fostering independence among different factors of variation in the learned representations, networks are able to focus on predictive factors while disregarding potential shortcuts during inference.

Through molecular simulations, we investigate the mechanisms of crystal nucleation in metal alloys and explore the relationship between nucleation and the glass transition, given that crystallization conditions often lie near this transition. Although lowering crystallization temperature typically reduces the free energy barrier, we observe an anomalous reversal in glass-forming alloys as the temperature approaches the glass transition point. Specifically, we simulated crystallization in two copper-based alloys: $Ag_6Cu_4$, which exhibits a positive heat of mixing, and $CuZn$, characterized by a large negative heat of mixing. Our findings reveal that this unusual behavior stems from a non-monotonic temperature dependence in the formation energy of connected icosahedral structures. These structures are incompatible with crystalline order, hinder nucleus development, and cause the free energy barrier to increase unexpectedly at low temperatures. Consequently, this promotes the formation of a predominantly closed-packed critical nucleus with fewer defects, offering a novel approach to controlling crystal nucleus structure—a factor of significant importance in catalysis.

This paper addresses the Byzantine reliable broadcast problem within authenticated and partially connected networks. Current state-of-the-art solutions typically merge two existing algorithms: Gabriel Bracha's authenticated double-echo broadcast protocol, which manages asynchrony and faulty senders under the assumption of a fully connected asynchronous network, and Danny Dolev's algorithm, which ensures reliable communication in a global fault model where up to $f$ processes among $N$ may fail in a network with at least $2f+1$ connectivity. Building on recent research demonstrating that Dolev's protocol benefits from various optimizations for practicality, we demonstrate that the leading methods for solving our specific problem can be further improved through layer-specific and cross-layer optimizations. Simulations conducted using the Omnet++ network simulator indicate that these optimizations can be effectively combined to significantly reduce both the total information transmitted and protocol latency. Specifically, with a 16-byte payload, $N=31$, and $f=4$, our approach achieves a 25% reduction in transmitted data and a 50% decrease in latency compared to the standard combination of Bracha's and Dolev's protocols.

This study revisits the evolutionary game theoretic frameworks developed by Antoci et al. (2016, 2018), which model dynamic outcomes resulting from interactions between patients and physicians facing clinical and legal risks. Specifically, Antoci et al. (2016) examined positive defensive medicine, whereas Antoci et al. (2018) focused on negative defensive medicine. We demonstrate that whenever these models possess a nonisochronous center, chaotic dynamics can be established for the associated Poincaré map using the Linked Twist Maps (LTMs) method. To achieve this, we apply a consistent rationale across both frameworks, leveraging the time-periodic variation of a model parameter that affects the center's position and reflects empirically supported seasonal risks in certain medical interventions. Additionally, we offer an ecological interpretation of the model, drawing on Harvie et al. (2007) to link it with intraspecific competition and environmental carrying capacity within predator-prey systems. In this context, it is reasonable to assume seasonal fluctuations in both carrying capacities and the intrinsic growth rates of the two populations. Although these parameters alter orbit shapes without shifting the center's location, we prove that chaotic dynamics for the corresponding Poincaré map still exist via the LTMs technique, despite the differing geometrical configuration of orbits in the phase plane.

Certain applications necessitate the complete removal of a sample's trace from a system, such as in response to deletion requests or the discovery of corrupted data. Merely deleting a sample from storage is insufficient because downstream machine learning models may retain information derived from it. Perfect unlearning occurs when all models trained on the sample are retrained from scratch without that sample. However, when multiple unlearning requests are anticipated, the cost of full retraining becomes prohibitive. Ensemble learning addresses this by partitioning training data into disjoint shards assigned to non-communicating weak learners, which are then aggregated into a central model. This approach creates a trade-off between performance and unlearning cost: smaller shards lower the cost of unlearning but may degrade performance. This paper introduces a coded learning protocol that employs linear encoders to partition training data into shards before the learning phase. We also detail a corresponding unlearning protocol that meets the criteria for perfect unlearning. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed coded machine unlearning achieves a superior balance between performance and unlearning cost compared to an uncoded baseline.

Although the catalog of confirmed exoplanets expands, the number of verified transiting planets orbiting evolved stars remains scarce. This study reports the discovery and confirmation of a hot Jupiter around TOI-2184 (TIC 176956893), a massive evolved subgiant ($M_\star= 1.53 \pm 0.12 M_\odot$, $R_\star= 2.90 \pm 0.14 R_\odot$) located within the $\textit{TESS}$ Southern Continuous Viewing Zone. Initially flagged as a false positive by the $\textit{TESS}$ Quick-Look Pipeline due to periodic systematics creating artificial depth variations between even and odd transits, the system was re-evaluated. By developing a new pipeline to eliminate background scattered light from $\textit{TESS}$ Full Frame Image (FFI) data, we integrated space-based $\textit{TESS}$ photometry, ground-based photometry, and radial velocity measurements to determine a planetary radius of $R_p= 1.017 \pm 0.051 R_J$ and a mass of $M_p= 0.65 \pm 0.16 M_J$. For an object so proximate to its host, TOI-2184b's mass and radius closely resemble those of Jupiter. However, the planet's radius is smaller than theoretical predictions based on its mass and incident flux, offering a significant new constraint on the timescale of post-main-sequence planet inflation. The identification of TOI-2184b proves that planets around faint stars ($\textit{TESS}$ magnitude $>12$) in the post-main sequence phase are detectable, suggesting that numerous similar systems await discovery in $\textit{TESS}$ FFIs; confirming these could clarify the final evolutionary stages of planetary systems.

This study examines Ramanujan congruences concerning the function that enumerates overpartitions of n featuring restricted odd differences. Specifically, we demonstrate that exactly one such congruence is present. Our approach employs modular forms theory to establish a broader theorem that limits the count of primes eligible for Ramanujan congruences within specific eta-quotients, thereby extending Jonah Sinick's research. Additionally, we present two congruences modulo 5 applicable to this function.

This letter examines the efficacy of covert communications employing faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling within a Rayleigh block fading channel, considering both Bayesian and Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence-based covertness constraints. Notably, for the KL divergence approach, we demonstrate that both the peak transmit power and the covert rate achievable with FTN signaling exceed those attainable with Nyquist signaling. Numerical simulations corroborate our theoretical findings, confirming the benefits of FTN signaling for secure data transmission.

Atomistic spin dynamics simulations investigate the demagnetization and associated magnetocaloric effect in strong-weak-strong ferromagnetic trilayers, specifically during the reorientation of the outer ferromagnets from a parallel to an antiparallel configuration. These simulations reveal non-trivial spin distributions within the antiparallel state, enabling direct entropy calculation. The resulting empirical models for magnetization distribution in the spacer layer differ substantially from commonly used theoretical models. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the magnetocaloric effect can be significantly enhanced by introducing spatial variations in local exchange interactions across the spacer, a strategy practically achievable through the tailored magnetic dilution of the spacer material.

The research community has increasingly focused on explainability for machine learning models to ensure the deployment of more reliable systems. In computer vision, generative counterfactual methods offer insights into a model's decision-making by showing how to perturb inputs to alter predictions. However, existing approaches often yield trivial counterfactuals by merely exaggerating or removing the classified attribute, which provides machine learning practitioners with little value regarding undesired biases in the model or data. This work addresses the issue of trivial counterfactual generation by proposing DiVE, which learns perturbations in a disentangled latent space. DiVE employs a diversity-enforcing loss to reveal multiple valuable explanations and includes a mechanism to specifically prevent the generation of trivial ones. Experiments on the CelebA and Synbols datasets show that DiVE outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods in producing high-quality, valuable explanations. The code is accessible at https://github.com/ElementAI/beyond-trivial-explanations.

The three primary families of hypergeometric orthogonal polynomials—Hermite, Laguerre, and Jacobi—govern the physical wavefunctions of bound stationary states in numerous quantum systems. The algebraic $\mathfrak{L}_{q}$-norms associated with these polynomials characterize various physical, chemical, and information-theoretic attributes of such systems, including kinetic and Weizsäcker energies, position and momentum expectation values, R\'enyi and Shannon entropies, as well as Cram\'er-Rao, Fisher-Shannon, and LMC complexity measures. This paper partially reviews and solves the $q$-asymptotics and parameter asymptotics (specifically when the weight function's parameter approaches infinity) for both unweighted and weighted $\mathfrak{L}_{q}$-norms of these orthogonal polynomials. The research is driven by the application of these algebraic norms to energetic, entropic, and complexity-related properties of highly-excited Rydberg states, high-dimensional pseudo-classical states within harmonic (oscillator-like) and Coulomb (hydrogenic) systems, and other quantum systems under central anharmonic potentials.

Stance classification is a critical task for analyzing argumentation in debates and identifying fake news; however, existing methods have primarily depended on models trained on individual debate topics. To develop a topic-independent system, this paper introduces a novel approach to generate a dataset with silver labels from raw text, which is then used to fine-tune a stance classification model. This extraction process leverages specific discourse relations, proven to be a reliable and accurate source for stance information. Furthermore, we propose a three-stage training framework where the noise level in the data decreases progressively from the first to the final stage. Experimental results demonstrate that both the automatically annotated dataset and the three-stage training strategy enhance model performance. Consequently, our method secured the first place among 26 teams in the stance classification track of the NLPCC 2021 shared task on Argumentative Text Understanding for AI Debater, validating the effectiveness of our approach.

This study examined how various training scenarios influence the prediction of chemical compound (retro)synthesis by utilizing text-based chemical reaction representations (SMILES) and a Transformer neural network architecture. We demonstrated that data augmentation—a technique prevalent in image processing—mitigated neural network memorization and enhanced performance in predicting new sequences. This improvement was observed specifically when augmentation was applied concurrently to both input and target data. On the USPTO-50k test dataset, a combination of SMILES augmentation and beam search achieved a top-5 accuracy of 84.8% for predicting the largest fragment, thereby identifying the principal transformation in classical retrosynthesis. This same approach yielded significantly superior results for predicting direct reactions within the single-step USPTO-MIT test set. Furthermore, our model attained 90.6% top-1 and 96.1% top-5 accuracy on its challenging mixed set, along with 97% top-5 accuracy for the USPTO-MIT separated set. It also substantially improved single-step retrosynthesis results on the USPTO-full set for both top-1 and top-10 metrics. Additionally, the frequency of appearance for the most frequently generated SMILES correlated well with prediction outcomes, serving as a viable metric for assessing reaction prediction quality.

The collection of indices identifying positive terms within a numerical sequence is known as its positivity set. This paper investigates the density of the positivity set for specific linear recurrence sequences, essentially determining the relative frequency of positive versus non-positive entries. We demonstrate that this density can be calculated to any desired level of accuracy and that it is possible to determine if the value is exactly zero or one. For diagonalisable sequences, we establish that the positivity set is finite if and only if the density equals zero. Additionally, we examine the arithmetic characteristics of these densities, proving that it is decidable whether the density is rational, provided the recurrence sequence possesses at most one pair of dominant complex roots. Finally, we extend these findings to symbolic orbits of linear dynamical systems, establishing that various properties of such systems can be decided up to a set of density zero.

We introduce the use of vector-valued distance to measure distances and derive geometric insights from the manifold of symmetric positive definite matrices (SPD), alongside the development of gyrovector calculus, which creates vector space operation analogs within this curved space. By implementing these operations, we demonstrate their adaptability in knowledge graph completion, item recommendation, and question answering tasks. Experimental results indicate that SPD models surpass their counterparts in Euclidean and hyperbolic spaces. Furthermore, the vector-valued distance enables the visualization of embeddings, revealing that the models successfully separate the representations of positive and negative samples.

We offer a succinct definition of an electromagnetic curve within a Riemannian manifold, demonstrating this concept through the specific example of a charged particle moving on a unit sphere subject to a uniform magnetic field.

Although electricity transmission expansion in Europe has faced numerous delays over recent decades—despite its critical role in integrating renewable energy—a hydrogen network leveraging existing fossil gas infrastructure could address this challenge. Such a network would not only supply low-emission fuels but also balance wind and solar fluctuations across the continent, potentially avoiding the need for extensive power grid upgrades. This study explores this concept by simulating net-zero CO$_2$ scenarios within a sector-coupled European energy system characterized by high renewable penetration and self-sufficiency. The model encompasses the electricity, buildings, transport, agriculture, and industrial sectors across 181 regions, operating at a resolution of every third hour throughout a year. This high spatio-temporal detail allows for the identification of transmission bottlenecks and the variability of both demand and renewable supply. The findings indicate a consistent advantage to a pan-continental hydrogen backbone that links high-yield areas with demand centers, synthetic fuel production facilities, and geological storage sites. Implementing a hydrogen network can reduce system costs by up to 6%, with the greatest savings occurring when electricity grid reinforcements are unfeasible. Between 58% and 66% of this backbone could be constructed using repurposed natural gas pipelines. However, the study concludes that hydrogen networks can only partially replace power grid expansion; the most significant cost reductions of 12% are achieved when both systems are developed together.

The nuclear level density (NLD) for $^{71}$Ga and $^{72}$Ga was derived using statistical model (SM) calculations based on $\gamma$-gated proton spectra from the reactions $^{64}$Ni($^{9}$Be, p2n)$^{70}$Ga and $^{64}$Ni($^{9}$Be, pn)$^{71}$Ga. These spectra are adequately described by a large inverse level density parameter ($k$ = 11.2 MeV) within the Fermi gas (FG) model framework, suggesting rotational enhancement consistent with findings in other mass regions. Alternatively, incorporating a rotational enhancement factor while maintaining a systematic $k$ value of 8.6 MeV also yields a satisfactory explanation of the spectral data, confirming the existence of collective enhancement in the NLD. This enhanced NLD was subsequently applied for the first time in TALYS calculations to determine the $^{71}$Ga(n, $\gamma$)$^{72}$Ga capture cross-section. Results indicate that the standard FG model underestimates capture data for $^{72}$Ga when collective enhancement is ignored, whereas including rotational enhancement leads to an overprediction at higher energies but provides an accurate description within the 0.01 to 0.1 MeV range. Consequently, the study demonstrates that accounting for collective enhancement is essential for accurately modeling low-energy capture cross-section data.

This paper examines the double scaling limit of two multi-matrix models: the $U(N)^2 \times O(D)$-invariant model featuring all quartic interactions and the bipartite $U(N) \times O(D)$-invariant model with tetrahedral interaction, where $D$ denotes the number of matrices and $N$ their dimension. Both systems support a simultaneous large $N$ and large $D$ expansion; while $N$ corresponds to the genus of Feynman graphs, $D$ corresponds to a quantity termed the grade. We reformulate the sum over Feynman graphs at fixed genus and grade as a finite sum over combinatorial schemes, a result of purely combinatorial nature that holds true in quantum mechanics and quantum field theory. We then analyze the double scaling limit at large $D$, specifically for vanishing grade. Our findings reveal that the most singular schemes in both models match those identified by Benedetti et al. for the $U(N)^2 \times O(D)$-invariant model restricted to tetrahedral interactions. This represents a distinct universality class compared to the 1-matrix model, whose double scaling is non-summable.

Inspired by Burillo, Cleary, and Roever's overview of obstructions within subgroups of Thompson's group $V$, we investigated higher-dimensional analogues, specifically the Brin-Thompson groups $nV$ and $SV$, as well as an infinite-dimensional class of Brin-Thompson groups and a specific subset of twisted variants denoted as $SV_G$ under particular conditions. Our findings indicate that these groups exhibit obstructions in their torsion subgroups similar to those found in Thompson's group $V$, while a notable selection of interesting Baumslag-Solitar groups are ruled out as subgroups of both $SV$ and $SV_G$. Furthermore, we briefly examine the group $\mathscr{S}V$, a broader class that relaxes certain "finiteness conditions," noting that some of these subgroup restrictions vanish in this context.

To ensure flight safety, air traffic control decision-support systems must enhance airspace capacity utilization and manage growing demand. This study tackles the challenge of aircraft conflict avoidance and trajectory recovery. Determining conflict-free paths with minimal deviation that ensure a return to target waypoints is highly complex due to the nonlinear nature of the trajectories involved. We introduce a two-stage iterative algorithm: the first stage resolves initial conflicts by adjusting speed and heading, while the second identifies the optimal time for each aircraft to recover toward its nominal path. The avoidance phase expands upon existing mixed-integer programming formulations, whereas the recovery phase proposes a new mixed-integer formulation. In this approach, speed and heading are modeled as continuous variables, while recovery time is treated as discrete. We demonstrate that anticipating trajectory recovery costs by allowing avoidance paths with greater deviation enables earlier recovery within a few iterations. Numerical experiments on benchmark conflict resolution problems indicate that this method can resolve instances involving up to 30 aircraft within 10 minutes.

The shift from paper records to Electronic Health Records (EHRs) has catalyzed significant progress in the modern healthcare sector.
