Frequently, patients must share these records with medical professionals. Given the sensitive and security-critical nature of EHRs, addressing the privacy and security challenges associated with their storage and dissemination is paramount. However, current security measures often involve encrypting the entire database, necessitating a full decryption process for every access request, which is computationally inefficient. Conversely, utilizing EHRs for medical research, such as precision medicine and diagnostics, alongside optimizing healthcare practices, demands that these records be easily analyzable without violating patient privacy. This paper introduces an efficient method named E-Tenon, which ensures all EHRs remain securely accessible to the public while delivering robust security features. To our knowledge, this represents the first application of an Open Database framework for EHR protection. E-Tenon enables patients to securely share their records under multi-level, fine-grained access policies they define themselves. Analysis demonstrates that our system surpasses existing solutions regarding computational complexity.

Analyzing longitudinal, heterogeneous, or unbalanced clustered data is crucial for numerous applications. The Linear Mixed Model (LMM) serves as a versatile extension of the linear model tailored specifically for these needs. Historically, much of the published literature on LMMs has focused on applying numerical optimization techniques—such as Newton-Raphson, Fisher Scoring, and Expectation Maximization—to single-factor models. Recently, however, research has shifted toward developing estimation and inference methods for more intricate, multi-factor designs. This paper introduces and derives new formulations extending the Fisher Scoring algorithm, traditionally used for single-factor LMM parameter estimation, to multiple crossed-factor designs. Using both simulated data and real-world examples, we evaluate five variants of the Fisher Scoring algorithm against each other and a baseline from the R package `lmer`, demonstrating that four of the proposed approaches are correct and computationally efficient. Furthermore, we propose a novel method for estimating Satterthwaite degrees of freedom in LMMs based on analytical results, eliminating the need for iterative gradient estimation. Simulation results indicate that this new approach yields estimates with reduced bias and variance compared to existing methods.

This work investigates the pseudoscalar mesons within the SU(3) linear sigma model using the Gaussian Functional Approximation (GFA). Employing a Lagrangian that features nonet scalar and pseudo-scalar mesons alongside symmetry breaking terms, we adopt a Gaussian Ansatz for the ground state wave function and utilize the variational method to minimize the ground state energy. This approach yields gap equations for the dressed meson masses, which serve as variational parameters in the GFA framework. Furthermore, we apply the Bethe-Salpeter equation to meson-meson scattering to determine the masses of the physical nonet mesons. To efficiently calculate the scattering T-matrix, we construct projection operators for flavor SU(3). Finally, the paper examines the characteristics of Nambu-Goldstone bosons across different limits of the chiral $U_L(3)\times U_R(3)$ symmetry.

This paper employs Sullivan's framework for the rational homotopy theory of simply-connected CW complexes of finite type to impose a graded commutative algebra structure on the $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $\mathcal{E}xt_{C^{\ast}(X;\mathbb{Q})}(\mathbb{Q},C^{\ast}(X;\mathbb{Q}))$. Consequently, we define the $\mathcal{E}xt$-based versions of higher (resp. module, homology) topological complexity for $X_0$, the rationalization of $X$ (resp. $X$ over $\mathbb{Q}$). We subsequently derive various inequalities relating these novel invariants to their classical counterparts within Gorenstein spaces. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of Adams-Hilton models (applicable to any coefficient field) by examining two specific scenarios: when the space is a 2-cell CW-complex and when it is a suspension.

We have created a technique to enable homodyne interferometers to maintain constant high sensitivity across numerous fringes for continuous real-time tracking. This approach extends the "J_1...J_4" methods, with its integration of Differential Wavefront Sensing to achieve highly sensitive angular measurements being straightforward. The system generates beams by applying a sinusoidal phase modulation of several radians to one arm of the interferometer. On a stable optical bench, we have demonstrated long-term sensitivity of 0.1 mrad/√Hz over thousands of seconds, which translates to 20 pm/√Hz in length and 10 nrad/√Hz in angle at millihertz frequencies.

The emergence of high-cadence, all-sky automated surveys has enabled the discovery of supernovae (SNe) closer to their explosion dates than ever before. Nevertheless, early pre-maximum light follow-up spectra for Type Ic supernovae (SNe Ic)—likely originating from the most stripped massive stars—remain scarce despite their significance. This study introduces a collection of 49 optical spectra acquired by the Las Cumbres Observatory via the Global Supernova Project for six SNe Ic, comprising 17 pre-maximum spectra, 8 of which were captured more than a week prior to V-band peak brightness. This dataset boosts the number of publicly available pre-maximum SNe Ic spectra by 25%, and we offer public SNID templates to facilitate the rapid identification of young SNe Ic in future observations. We provide a detailed analysis of these spectra, covering Fe II 5169 velocity measurements, O I 7774 line strengths, and continuum morphologies. Comparing our findings with existing literature on stripped supernovae, we identify one outlier: SN 2019ewu. This object exhibits a distinctive set of characteristics for an SNe Ic, including an exceptionally blue continuum, high absorption velocities, and a P-cygni profile appearing nearly two weeks before maximum light that TARDIS radiative transfer modeling suggests corresponds to C II rather than H$\alpha$. Furthermore, SN 2019ewu shows weak or absent O I 7774 absorption until the time of maximum light.

Blue horizontal-branch (BHB) stars serve as valuable tracers for investigating the Milky Way's formation and structure due to their advanced age. To compile a pristine catalogue of these stars, we initially cross-matched the Gaia Data Release 2 (DR2) with established reference catalogues to establish selection criteria using Gaia DR2 parameters. These methods were later validated and applied to the more recent Gaia Early Data Release 3 (EDR3). The objective of this study is to produce a catalogue of BHB candidates selected via photometric and astrometric data that minimizes contamination. Our approach involved cross-matching reference BHB datasets with the Gaia DR2 database to define two distinct selection criteria: one utilizing colour and absolute G magnitude, and another using colour and reduced proper motion. While focusing on the Galactic halo—where young main-sequence stars are scarce—reduced main-sequence contamination was achieved, albeit with a trade-off in completeness. The final EDR3-based catalogue comprises 57,377 BHB stars; specifically, 16,794 candidates were identified using Gaia EDR3 parallaxes, while an additional 40,583 were selected based on their proper motions.

Classical statistics establishes that an experiment involving $n$ independent and identically distributed observations from $d$-dimensional multinomial distributions is well-approximated by a $(d-1)$-dimensional Gaussian distribution. In the quantum realm, it was previously demonstrated that a collection of $n$ full-rank qudits can be approximated by a hybrid system comprising a $(d-1)$-dimensional Gaussian component and a quantum component consisting of an ensemble of $d(d-1)/2$ shifted thermal states. This paper extends that finding to scenarios where the qudits are not of full rank. We demonstrate that when the qudit rank is $r$, the limiting experiment comprises an $(r-1)$-dimensional Gaussian distribution alongside an ensemble of both shifted pure and shifted thermal states. Furthermore, we propose a two-stage estimation procedure for low-rank qudits, yielding an estimator that is sharp minimax optimal. Additionally, for estimating a linear functional of the quantum state, we construct an estimator, evaluate its risk, and utilize quantum LAN to prove its minimax optimality.

This paper introduces a new state representation for reward-free Markov decision processes. The core concept involves self-supervised learning of an embedding space where the distance between embedded states reflects the minimum number of actions required to transition between them. Unlike prior methods, our approach requires no domain knowledge and learns effectively from offline, unlabeled data. We demonstrate how this representation facilitates the learning of goal-conditioned policies by establishing state-goal similarity and offering a heuristic distance metric to guide planning and reinforcement learning. Empirical validation across classic control tasks and multi-goal environments confirms that our method successfully learns representations within large and/or continuous domains.

Ad hoc teamwork addresses the challenge of creating agents capable of collaborating with unfamiliar partners without any pre-established coordination. This survey offers a dual contribution: initially, it presents an organized overview of the various dimensions inherent to the ad hoc teamwork problem; subsequently, it examines advancements achieved within the field and highlights both current and future unresolved issues that require attention.

Detecting sclerotic bone metastases in Computed Tomography (CT) scans holds significant promise for clinical and research applications. Current state-of-the-art techniques achieve a sensitivity of 79% with 10 false positives per volume. To improve upon this, we propose a two-tiered coarse-to-fine cascade framework. The first tier employs a highly sensitive candidate generation system operating at approximately 92% sensitivity, albeit with a higher false positive rate of around 50 per patient, to identify Regions of Interest (ROIs). These ROIs serve as inputs for the second tier, where N 2D views are synthesized through random scaling, translation, and rotation around each ROI centroid. These varied views train a deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) classifier. During testing, the CNN evaluates a new set of N random views for each ROI, averaging their probabilities to determine a final classification score. This selective second stage effectively filters out difficult false positives while maintaining high sensitivity. Validated on CT data from 59 patients (49 with metastases and 10 controls), the method significantly reduces false positives per volume, decreasing counts from 4 to 1.2, 7 to 3, and 12 to 9.5 at sensitivity levels of 60%, 70%, and 80%, respectively. With an Area-Under-the-Curve (AUC) of 0.834, these results demonstrate a marked improvement over previous approaches.

This study tackles attitude estimation for rigid bodies utilizing potentially time-varying vector measurements, establishing a necessary and sufficient condition for distinguishability. This new condition is demonstrated to be strictly less restrictive than those previously applied in attitude observer design. Furthermore, it is shown that even with a single vector measurement, this condition suffices to construct almost globally convergent attitude observers, with two explicit designs derived. To address weak excitation, the first approach leverages historical data, while the second dynamically generates a virtual reference vector that maintains non-collinearity with the measured vector. Simulation outcomes confirm accurate estimation even in the presence of noisy measurements.
A novel and straightforward proof is presented for counting labeled rooted forest-graphs with a specific number of vertices. Cayley's formula emerges as a specific instance of this general result.

Focus-based techniques have yielded encouraging outcomes for depth estimation; however, most current approaches rely heavily on the maximum sharpness within the focal stack, leaving out-of-focus information underutilized. This paper introduces a dynamically multimodal learning strategy that integrates RGB data with the focal stack. By developing a spatial correlation perception module, we aim to thoroughly analyze spatial relationships within the focal stack, while a multimodal dynamic fusion module adaptively merges this information with RGB data. Our method achieves state-of-the-art results on two benchmark datasets. Additionally, testing on images captured by a smartphone camera demonstrates that our approach overcomes the reliance on light field data, paving the way for practical depth estimation applications on common consumer cameras.

WEAVE represents a new wide-field spectroscopy facility installed at the prime focus of the William Herschel Telescope on La Palma, Spain. Its fibre positioner is critical for the precise positioning of the spectrograph's 960-fibre multiplex. This overview details recent maintenance activities, flexure adjustments, and calibration measurements performed at the observatory before the final top-end assembly. These efforts ensure a comprehensive understanding of the positioner's behavior across various orientations during observations. All fibre systems have been examined and repaired, and the tumbler structure now features new clamps designed to stiffen both the internal beam and the retractor support disk, which holds the field plates. We present updated metrology procedures and results that are scheduled for on-sky verification.

This study examines the tensor eigenvalue complementarity problem (TEiCP), which emerges in the stability analysis of finite-dimensional mechanical systems and is intrinsically linked to the optimality conditions of polynomial optimization. The paper explores two monotone ascent spectral projected gradient (SPG) approaches for solving TEiCP. Additionally, we introduce a shifted scaling-and-projection algorithm (SPA), representing a significant enhancement over the original SPA method developed by Ling, He, and Qi. Numerical experiments comparing these proposed techniques with existing gradient methods from the literature are provided to demonstrate their efficiency.

This work establishes the existence and stability of smooth solutions for the steady Navier-Stokes equations in the vicinity of plane Poiseuille-Couette flow. As a result, we also derive the zero viscosity limit for the 2D steady Navier-Stokes equations, showing their convergence to the steady Euler equations. Initially, without external forces, we demonstrate the existence of smooth, stable solutions under infinitesimal perturbations of plane Poiseuille-Couette flow. Specifically, for Couette flow as the base state, stability is proven for sufficiently small finite perturbations. Furthermore, by applying an appropriate external force to regulate the flow, we obtain a broad class of smooth, stable solutions with respect to infinitesimal variations in that force. Finally, utilizing the same linear estimates, we confirm that all aforementioned solutions converge to Euler equation solutions in the zero viscosity limit.

We have constructed families of non-toric $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal Fano ($\mathbb{Q}$-Fano) threefolds with codimensions of at least 20, which correspond to 54 mutation classes of rigid maximally mutable Laurent polynomials. In the context of mirror symmetry, these represent the highest codimension (non-toric) $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano varieties for which the Fano/Landau-Ginzburg correspondence is currently known. Additionally, we have created 46 more $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano threefolds, with their codimensions spanning new examples from 19 down to 10. Some of these varieties are presented as toric complete intersections, while others are defined as Pfaffian varieties.

We investigated the optical and electrical spectra of an n-i-p LED containing three GaAs quantum wells within its intrinsic region, varying the applied magnetic field. Due to excess n-type doping, these quantum wells hosted a two-dimensional Landau electron gas. As the magnetic field increased, the initial broad emission band at zero field transformed into distinct features corresponding to interband transitions between Landau levels of different indices (l) associated with the sub-bands, adhering to specific selection rules. For each transition, an energy splitting between the two polarized components was detected, matching the sum of the spin splittings in the conduction and valence bands. By utilizing the known electron g-factor, we calculated the valence band spin splittings. A comparison between our experimental results and numerical calculations revealed reasonable agreement.

Accurate position measurement is fundamental to cavity quantum optomechanics, serving as the basis for numerous sensing applications and fundamental physics tests. Notably, multiple optomechanical experiments are now transitioning into a highly desirable nonlinear regime characterized by strong optomechanical interactions even at low light intensities. While this regime promises novel quantum phenomena and enhanced performance, a dedicated methodology for mechanical position measurement and its associated theoretical framework are required to fully exploit these potentials. In this work, we establish a cavity quantum optomechanics framework that accounts for the nonlinearities inherent in both radiation-pressure interactions and cavity responses, proposing specific strategies for position measurement within this context. Our approach employs optical heterodyne detection schemes, spanning single to dual homodyne methods, to extract mechanical position data encoded in the optical amplitude and phase quadratures, supporting both pulsed and continuous operational modes. As experimental efforts increasingly encounter these cavity optomechanical nonlinearities, our framework will facilitate significant advancements in areas such as quantum metrology, investigations of the standard quantum limit, and quantum measurement and control.

Comprehending the influence of external initiatives and events on Wikipedia's readership is vital for enhancing content visibility and accessibility. This study explores the development of time-series models designed to forecast Wikipedia page views, specifically to identify significant deviations from established trends. We evaluate these models using data from two distinct events: a video campaign intended to boost awareness of Hindi Wikipedia within India, and the implementation of a page preview feature that allows users to access content without visiting the full pages, tested on English and German editions. While our models successfully quantify the impact of the page preview rollout, they fail to detect a notable shift following the video campaign in India. Additionally, we examine the potential of leveraging data from other regions or language editions to predict page view metrics for specific areas and language versions.

Predictive Process Monitoring is a domain within Process Mining focused on forecasting the future trajectory of an active business process based on historical data from event logs. The growing body of literature in this area highlights a demand for tools that assist researchers and users in evaluating, comparing, and selecting the most appropriate techniques. Nirdizati is a specialized platform designed to help users construct, compare, analyze, and interpret predictive models for forecasting the evolution of ongoing cases. By offering a comprehensive suite of state-of-the-art methods, Nirdizati serves as a versatile and practical resource for BPM practitioners and academics to explore and benchmark Predictive Process Monitoring approaches. This paper introduces the latest version of Nirdizati, detailing an architecture engineered to enhance modularity and scalability. The tool's extensive feature set empowers researchers and practitioners throughout the entire workflow of developing robust Predictive Process Monitoring models.

We examine interacting one-dimensional bosons within the universal low-energy regime, where interactions comprise both attractive and repulsive components capable of stabilizing quantum gases, droplets, and liquids. Specifically, we investigate the impact of effective three-body repulsion in systems characterized by weak pairwise attraction. While the low-energy behavior is frequently posited to be equivalent to a model featuring only non-zero-range two-body interactions, our findings at zero temperature reveal that the equations of state align quantitatively at low densities in the overall repulsive gas phase, as predicted by the $S$-matrix formulation of statistical mechanics. Conversely, this equivalence breaks down in the attractive regime, where universality is restricted to the long-distance characteristics of quantum droplets. By developing analytical tools to explore the theory, we achieve remarkable agreement with precise numerical results derived from the density-matrix renormalization group.

We derive a priori $L^\infty$ estimates for a broad class of fully nonlinear partial differential equations involving $(n-1)$-forms on compact Hermitian manifolds. This approach utilizes a local comparison technique with auxiliary Monge-Ampère equations, previously established by B. Guo and D. H. Phong. The central challenge involves identifying the suitable elliptic operator that allows the maximum principle to hold.

We establish a polyhedral description of the Jelonek set for polynomial maps $f:K^n\to K^n$ defined over an algebraically closed field with characteristic zero, where this set comprises the points where $f$ fails to be finite. By examining the tropical counterpart of the Jelonek set, we demonstrate a correspondence theorem linking classical and tropical polynomial maps. This framework enables a re-proof of the $K$-uniruleness of the Jelonek set and facilitates the calculation of its tropical hypersurface using polyhedral techniques. Additionally, we illustrate how these findings allow for the recovery of the face-lattice of the Newton polytope associated with the Jelonek set for a broad class of complex polynomial maps.

Beginning with unitary quantum dynamics, we examine the integration of quantum measurements, which consist of four key elements: bifurcation, witness generation, an alignment projection, and the final choice selection. The initial two elements remain within the realm of unitary dynamics. The third component is accounted for by the concept of decoherence, grounded in the condition that wave function and conjugate witnesses at the temporal endpoint must be identical, thereby maintaining the framework within quantum dynamics. The fourth element, the actual choice, is explained by the surjection hypothesis, which utilizes a two-boundary interpretation of the entire quantum universe. This approach provides a straightforward method to transform what appear to be random projections into purely deterministic unitary quantum dynamics, effectively resolving the measurement problem.

Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has significantly advanced numerous artificial intelligence domains, such as gaming, robotics, pattern recognition, and recommendation systems. Likewise, graph neural networks (GNN) have proven highly effective in supervised learning tasks involving graph-structured data. Recently, combining GNN with DRL for environments defined by graph structures has garnered substantial interest. This paper offers a comprehensive survey of these hybrid approaches, categorizing them into two types: (1) algorithmic enhancement, where DRL and GNN complement one another to improve utility, and (2) application-specific enhancement, where the two methods mutually support specific use cases. This integration effectively tackles complex challenges in engineering and the life sciences. Building on this review, we examine the advantages and applicability of merging these fields, particularly regarding enhanced generalizability and reduced computational complexity. Finally, we outline the primary challenges in integrating DRL and GNN and suggest potential future research directions, topics of relevance to the wider machine learning community.

This study evaluates the validity of video recreations as a baseline alternative to live settings for shoulder surfing attacks. We replicated a subset of factors from Aviv et al.'s (ACSAC 2017) video-simulation experiment but replaced the simulation with a live study involving 36 participants (where both victims and attackers were present). The results indicate that for Android graphical patterns, video simulations align with live settings regarding attacker success rates. However, statistically significant differences emerged for both 4- and 6-digit PINs, with live attackers achieving success rates up to 1.9 times higher than in video simulations. While the security advantages of removing feedback lines in Android patterns are significantly reduced in live scenarios—especially under multiple observations—the data supports using video recreations as a baseline for attacker success rates. Nevertheless, researchers are cautioned that these baselines may substantially underestimate the threat posed by attackers in real-world live environments.

Accurately identifying affiliations within scholarly publication metadata is essential for tracking and analyzing scientific trends, particularly within open science frameworks. We introduce a modular, Elasticsearch-based approach for automatic alignment against registries, which delegates the selection of alignment criteria to the user, thereby granting them direct control over the method's precision and recall. This paper presents an implementation that performs automatic alignment across three registries—countries, GRID.ac, and the French research laboratory directory (RNSR)—with code available at https://github.com/dataesr/matcher and a detailed performance analysis provided herein.

Diaconis and Gamburd previously calculated moments of secular coefficients within the CUE ensemble. By utilizing the characteristic map, we provide an alternative combinatorial proof of their findings. Furthermore, we broaden their computation to include moments of traces of symmetric powers; although the results remain consistent, this extension applies to a broader range. Our combinatorial approach draws inspiration from gcd matrices, as previously employed by Vaughan and Wooley, and by Granville and Soundararajan. Leveraging these CUE calculations, we propose a conjecture regarding moments of character sums twisted by the Möbius function and demonstrate a specific instance of this conjecture within function fields.

Quantified CTL (QCTL) is an established temporal logic that augments standard CTL with quantification over atomic propositions. Recently, it has emerged as a potent framework for investigating logics of strategic reasoning. We broaden this logic to accommodate imperfect information by parameterizing its quantifiers with specific observations that dictate the extent of model visibility, thereby restricting their behavior. We analyze two distinct semantic interpretations: one corresponding to no memory and the other to perfect recall. Regarding expressiveness, we demonstrate that the logic aligns with Monadic Second-Order (MSO) logic under the no-memory semantics, and with MSO logic of equal level under the perfect recall semantics. Furthermore, we prove that the model-checking problem is Pspace-complete for the no-memory semantics. Although the problem is undecidable for the perfect recall semantics, we identify a decidable syntactic fragment defined by hierarchical formulas, establishing its decidability through an automata-theoretic method.

We introduce CQELS 2.0, the second iteration of the Continuous Query Evaluation over Linked Streams framework, which serves as a platform-agnostic, federated execution system designed for semantic stream fusion. This release features a new neural-symbolic stream reasoning module that facilitates the definition of deep neural network (DNN) data fusion pipelines using logic rules where learnable probabilistic values act as weights. As a framework independent of specific hardware, CQELS 2.0 supports deployment across diverse architectures, ranging from embedded devices to cloud infrastructure. Additionally, the updated version incorporates an adaptive federator that enables CQELS instances on various network nodes to coordinate resources by distributing processing pipelines; this is achieved by delegating partial workloads to peer nodes through the subscription of continuous queries.

Edge TPUs serve as specialized accelerators designed for low-power edge devices and are integral to numerous Google products, including Coral and Pixel hardware. This paper begins by examining the primary microarchitectural features of Edge TPUs. It then conducts a comprehensive evaluation of three distinct Edge TPU classes—spanning various computing ecosystems and representing both current Google deployments and future product pipelines—across a dataset of 423,000 unique convolutional neural networks. Based on this extensive analysis, we provide critical and interpretable microarchitectural insights regarding the performance of these Edge TPU classes across diverse neural network structures. Furthermore, we detail our ongoing work in creating high-accuracy learned machine learning models to predict key accelerator performance metrics, such as latency and energy consumption. These models facilitate significantly faster evaluations, reducing assessment time to the millisecond range as a more efficient alternative to time-intensive cycle-accurate simulators, thereby opening new avenues for rapid hardware/software co-design.

Analyzing broad trends in student course registration holds significant value for university administrators and educational researchers. However, critical decisions are frequently made lacking a solid quantitative framework for the mechanisms driving student choices. This paper introduces a probabilistic method for modeling enrollment decisions, inspired by multilabel classification and mixture models. Utilizing a decade of anonymized transcripts from a major institution, we developed a Gaussian latent variable model to capture the joint distribution of course selections. These models support various inference queries and maintain robustness against data sparsity. We validate the approach's effectiveness against alternatives, including deep learning structures, and show its capacity to deduce the underlying student interests that influence enrollment choices.

This study explores machine learning models designed to classify online interactions marked by subtle forms of abuse, including hostility, sarcasm, and generalization. Utilizing a public dataset of 44,000 comments labeled as either healthy or unhealthy across seven distinct toxicity categories, the research achieved micro F1-score, macro F1-score, and ROC-AUC values of 88.76%, 67.98%, and 0.71, respectively. The analysis indicates that hostile remarks were the most readily identifiable among unhealthy comments. Additionally, sentiment analysis demonstrated that unhealthy comments generally exhibit a slight negative tone, with hostility showing the strongest negative sentiment.

We present a method for constructing completions of affine spaces into the total spaces of $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal Mori fiber spaces over the projective line. As an application, we provide families of examples featuring general fibers that are non-rational, birationally rigid, and non-stably rational.

Learning from Positive and Unlabeled (PU) data involves training models using only positive and unlabeled samples, as negative examples remain unknown. This setting is critical for tasks like medical diagnosis, social network analysis, financial market evaluation, and knowledge base completion, all of which often suffer from intrinsic imbalance, where negative instances vastly outnumber positives. However, most current PU learning approaches are evaluated on artificially balanced datasets, leaving their performance on realistic, imbalanced, and long-tail distributions unclear. To address this, we propose a robust and efficient self-supervised pretraining strategy. We demonstrate that conventional self-supervised methods require reformulation when applied to highly imbalanced PU distributions. Consequently, we introduce \textit{ImPULSeS}, a unified representation learning framework for \underline{Im}balanced \underline{P}ositive \underline{U}nlabeled \underline{L}earning that leverages \underline{Se}lf-\underline{S}upervised debiased pre-training. ImPULSeS combines large-scale unsupervised learning with a debiased contrastive loss and an additional reweighted PU loss. Experiments across multiple datasets reveal that ImPULSeS reduces the error rate of the previous state-of-the-art by half, even outperforming methods provided with the true prior. Furthermore, our method exhibits enhanced robustness against prior misspecification and superior performance when pretraining occurs on unrelated datasets. We anticipate that this robustness and efficiency will facilitate practitioners in achieving excellent results on various PU datasets. The source code is available at \url{https://github.com/JSchweisthal/ImPULSeS}.

Robotic temporal logic planning encounters state explosion when dealing with specifications containing numerous discrete locations. We introduce a novel method, specifically designed for universally quantified location tasks, which achieves constant time complexity relative to the number of locations, thus allowing plan synthesis for any scale. Our proposed hybrid control framework employs an iterator to manage the discretized workspace, effectively shielding it from a discrete event controller executing the plan. Although this approach introduces increased execution overhead, we demonstrate that this cost remains reasonable for fixed-wing Unmanned Aerial Vehicle missions in both simulated and real-world settings, supporting up to 700,000 locations.

The significance of a concept is determined by its context. This context consists of two elements: the identity of the tokens and their structural arrangement (topology). We contend that a position-based approach is both more versatile and advantageous. Traditional NLP objectives like MLM and CLM can be straightforwardly formulated as predicting positions across the entire vocabulary. By adapting the paradigm of relative position encoding to generate relative labels for self-supervised learning, we aim to demonstrate that this method yields superior pre-training results, as evidenced by performance on downstream tasks.

This work generalizes the quandle cocycle invariant to encompass stuck links. Specifically, we introduce an invariant for stuck links by assigning Boltzmann weights to both standard and stuck crossings. As a practical application, we establish single-variable and two-variable polynomial invariants for stuck links. Additionally, we define corresponding single-variable and two-variable polynomial invariants for arc diagrams representing RNA foldings. Finally, we present explicit calculations for these newly defined invariants.

Reconstructing and aligning dense 3D faces in uncontrolled environments presents significant difficulties due to missing facial data caused by occlusions and extreme head poses, which further expand the solution space and complicate modeling. Our approach addresses these challenges by modeling occlusion and pose variations to decompose the complex task into several more tractable subproblems. Consequently, we introduce an end-to-end framework called Self-aligned Dual face Regression Network (SADRNet), which simultaneously predicts both pose-dependent and pose-independent facial representations. These predictions are fused via an occlusion-aware self-alignment mechanism to produce the final 3D face. Comprehensive experiments on two widely used benchmarks, AFLW2000-3D and Florence, show that our method significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches.

We introduce Low Distortion Local Eigenmaps (LDLE), a manifold learning approach that builds a collection of low-distortion, lower-dimensional local views of a dataset and aligns them to create a global embedding. These local views are generated from the global eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian and aligned via Procrustes analysis, with the specific eigenvectors potentially varying by region. Unlike current methods, LDLE can embed closed and non-orientable manifolds into their intrinsic dimension by temporarily separating them, while also offering gluing instructions at the boundaries of the torn embedding to assist in identifying the original topology. Our experiments demonstrate that LDLE effectively preserves distances up to a constant scale, outperforming other techniques that result in greater distortion. Furthermore, we show that LDLE generates high-quality embeddings even when dealing with noisy or sparse data.

The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) offers the capability to investigate the atmospheric compositions and surface characteristics of hot, rocky worlds using emission spectroscopy. We have pinpointed 18 promising terrestrial planet candidates discovered by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) that are well-suited for such studies. These candidates span a wide spectrum of radii ($R_{\rm p} \sim 0.6 - 2.0 R_\oplus$) and orbit stars with diverse properties, including magnitudes ($K_s = 5.78 - 10.78$, $V = 8.4 - 15.69$) and effective temperatures ($T_{\rm eff} \sim 3000 - 6000$ K). Leveraging ground-based data from the TESS Follow-up Observing Program (TFOP) alongside the vetting algorithms DAVE and TRICERATOPS, we evaluated the likelihood of these candidates being genuine planets. Our analysis confirmed 13 planets: TOI-206 b, TOI-500 b, TOI-544 b, TOI-833 b, TOI-1075 b, TOI-1411 b, TOI-1442 b, TOI-1693 b, TOI-1860 b, TOI-2260 b, TOI-2411 b, TOI-2427 b, and TOI-2445 b. Among these, seven (TOI-206 b, TOI-500 b, TOI-1075 b, TOI-1442 b, TOI-2260 b, TOI-2411 b, and TOI-2445 b) are ultra-short-period planets. Notably, TOI-1860 represents the youngest solar twin with a confirmed planet ($133 \pm 26$ Myr), while TOI-2260 is a young ($321 \pm 96$ Myr), metal-rich G dwarf ($[\text{Fe/H}] = 0.22 \pm 0.06$ dex) hosting an ultra-short-period planet. Furthermore, given its estimated equilibrium temperature of approximately 2600 K, TOI-2260 b ranks as the fourth hottest known planet with a radius under $2 \, R_\oplus$.

This work introduces a scalable graphical approach for selecting and partitioning datasets to optimize the training phase of classification tasks. The proposed heuristic relies on a clustering algorithm, chosen specifically to ensure that its computational cost remains proportional to the task at hand. Following clustering, an information graph representing the underlying classification patterns is constructed using approximate nearest neighbor techniques. The method comprises two distinct strategies: one for reducing the size of a given training set and another for partitioning the resulting reduced or selected set. Designed for large datasets, the primary objective is to substantially decrease training computation time without sacrificing prediction accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that both strategies significantly accelerate the training process compared to state-of-the-art shrinking heuristics available in LIBSVM, while maintaining prediction accuracy that closely matches or exceeds those methods. Additionally, a network architecture is proposed to support distributed training based on the partitioning formulation, yielding further reductions in training runtime relative to serial implementations of the approaches.

This study employs the Butterfly Optimization Algorithm (BOA) introduced in [1] to fine-tune the parameters of a designed Lead-Lag Controller, aiming to achieve system stability. A numerical evaluation of BOA was conducted and benchmarked against established methods, specifically the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Differential Evolution (DE). The analysis indicates that while BOA outperforms the others in eigenvalue analysis, its capability in optimizing the minimum damping coefficient is comparable to that of GA and DE.

From the third Swift-BAT catalog, we have chosen 52 long gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) that exhibit precursor activity. The Norris function was applied to fit every episode observed in both the precursors and the main bursts, allowing for a systematic analysis of their temporal characteristics. Our investigation reveals no significant distinction between the temporal profiles of the precursors and the main bursts. Additionally, the photon counts of the precursors correlate with those of the main bursts. This correlation, along with the fact that both components adhere to the same $\tau_p-\omega$ relation, suggests a common physical origin for the precursors and main bursts. However, no explicit relationship was found between the energy released during the precursor phase and the quiescent time. Theoretical frameworks, including the fallback collapsar and jet-cocoon scenarios, could offer valuable insights into explaining GRB precursor phenomena.

Active inference serves as a leading framework for modeling brain mechanisms, including curiosity, habit formation, and dopaminergic activity. However, current implementations face exponential complexity when calculating priors across all possible policies up to a specific time horizon. To address this, Fountas et al. (2020) employed Monte Carlo tree search, achieving strong results on two tasks. Meanwhile, Champion et al. (2021a) introduced a tree search method grounded in temporal structure learning, made possible by a variational message passing approach for active inference that facilitates the compositional construction of Bayesian networks. We refer to this message-passing tree search as branching-time active inference (BTAI), though it has lacked empirical validation. This paper presents an experimental evaluation of BTAI using a maze-solving agent, demonstrating that improved prior preferences and deeper search depths reduce vulnerability to local minima. We further compare BTAI against standard active inference (AcI) on graph navigation tasks. While both methods succeed on small graphs, AcI becomes intractable due to exponential space complexity on larger graphs, whereas BTAI scales efficiently by exploring the policy space more effectively. Additionally, we compared BTAI to the POMCP algorithm in the Frozen Lake environment; results indicate that both agents accumulate comparable rewards, with specific conditions identified where one outperforms the other. Finally, we evaluated BTAI against the approach of Fountas et al. (2020) on the dSprites dataset, discussing the respective advantages and limitations of each method.

This research investigates the simultaneous breaking of spatial translations and dilatations within Ginzburg-Landau-like models, where symmetry breaking dynamics are governed by an effective Mexican hat potential for spatial gradients. We demonstrate the existence of fractonic modes characterized by either subdimensional propagation or complete immobility. This category of effective field theories includes helical superfluids and meta-fluids, where fractons arise from an emergent symmetry involving higher-moment charges, consequently trivializing certain elastic coefficients. Introducing a finite charge density modifies fracton mobility and creates a competition between the chemical potential and superfluid velocity in setting the dilaton gap. Furthermore, fracton mobility can be altered even at zero density by incorporating additional higher-derivative terms.

Most datasets include both continuous and categorical variables, yet modeling high-dimensional mixed predictors in regression and classification statistics has seen little attention. This paper addresses the general regression challenge of inferring a variable of interest using high-dimensional mixed continuous and binary predictors. The objective is to identify a lower-dimensional function of the mixed predictor vector that encapsulates all modeling information regarding the response, whether continuous or categorical. Our proposed approach identifies sufficient reductions by reversing the regression process, instead modeling the mixed predictors conditional on the response. We derive the maximum likelihood estimator for these sufficient reductions, develop asymptotic tests for dimensionality, and introduce a regularized estimator that simultaneously performs variable selection and dimension reduction. Finally, we evaluate the method's performance through simulations and real-world data comparisons against other approaches.

In numerous computer graphics, artistic, and design contexts, there is a strong desire for users to supply intuitive non-visual inputs—such as text, sketches, strokes, graphs, or layouts—and for systems to automatically produce photorealistic images that respect this content. Although traditional approaches to automatic image generation relied on image retrieval and composition, recent breakthroughs in deep generative models, including generative adversarial networks (GANs), variational autoencoders (VAEs), and flow-based methods, have unlocked more robust and flexible image creation capabilities. This paper surveys recent literature on synthesizing images from intuitive user inputs, examining progress in input versatility, generation techniques, benchmark datasets, and evaluation metrics. These developments inspire new viewpoints regarding input representation and interactivity, the integration of major image generation paradigms, and the comparative assessment of generation methods.

Although Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) deliver high classification accuracy on numerous large-scale real-world datasets, they lack a rigorous framework for quantifying predictive uncertainty. By utilizing recent progress in conformal prediction, we develop prediction sets for node classification within inductive learning settings and validate our method's effectiveness across standard benchmark datasets using established GNN architectures. The implementation can be accessed at the provided link.

Chiral Higher Spin Gravity, incorporating a cosmological constant, is formulated as a Free Differential Algebra at the level of its equations of motion, representing a smooth deformation of its flat-space counterpart (arXiv:2205.07794). As a distinct class of local higher spin theories, the existence of Chiral Higher Spin Gravity suggests the presence of a closed, and likely integrable, sub-sector within Chern-Simons Matter Theories. This discovery carries significant implications for both the theoretical frameworks themselves and for the understanding of three-dimensional bosonization duality.

This research investigates how networked agents collaborate to estimate a dynamical state of nature given partial information. The authors introduce a distributed Bayesian filtering algorithm designed for finite-state hidden Markov models (HMMs), applicable to both sequential state estimation and modeling opinion dynamics within social networks under changing conditions. The study demonstrates that the deviation from an optimal centralized solution remains asymptotically bounded for geometrically ergodic state transition models, encompassing those that change rapidly. Additionally, recursions for computing error probabilities are derived, and convergence is proven under Gaussian observation models. Simulations are included to validate the theoretical findings and benchmark the approach against other methods.

The growing integration of Machine Learning (ML) components into autonomous systems, known as Learning-Enabled Systems (LESs), has created an urgent requirement to ensure their functional safety. Consistent with traditional functional safety practices, both industry and academia now agree that assurance cases are essential for this goal. These cases typically support reliability claims that underpin safety, serving as a structured method to organize arguments and evidence derived from safety analysis and reliability modeling. Although assurance activities have historically followed consensus-based standards rooted in extensive engineering experience, LESs present unique challenges in safety-critical applications due to the specific characteristics and design of ML models. This article introduces a comprehensive assurance framework for LESs, with a focus on quantitative elements such as decomposing system-level safety targets into component-level requirements and validating claims based on reliability metrics. We subsequently present a novel, model-agnostic Reliability Assessment Model (RAM) for ML classifiers that leverages operational profiles and robustness verification evidence. We examine the model's assumptions, the inherent difficulties in assessing ML reliability revealed by our RAM, and propose practical solutions. Furthermore, we develop probabilistic safety argument templates at the lower ML component level based on the RAM. To validate and demonstrate our approach, we conduct experiments on synthetic and benchmark datasets, as well as case studies involving simulated Autonomous Underwater Vehicles and physical Unmanned Ground Vehicles.

Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) are widely recognized for experiencing performance decline as network depth increases, a phenomenon typically blamed on over-smoothing. However, despite this prevailing view, we identify a gap between current theoretical interpretations of over-smoothing and the actual behavior of GCNs. Specifically, we contend that over-smoothing does not inevitably occur in practice; instead, deeper GCNs are provably expressive, capable of converging to a global optimum with a linear rate, and able to attain high training accuracy when trained correctly. Although these deep models can achieve superior training performance, empirical evidence reveals they generalize poorly on test sets, leaving the theoretical explanation for this behavior unclear. To address this, we rigorously analyze the generalization properties of GCNs, demonstrating that the training strategies used to maximize accuracy significantly compromise generalization. Guided by these insights, we introduce a decoupled GCN architecture that separates weight matrices from feature propagation to maintain expressiveness while ensuring robust generalization. We validate our theoretical claims through extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

In asymptotically flat gauge and gravitational theories, infinitely many conserved charges arise from large gauge transformations or diffeomorphisms at infinity. While some literature suggests these charges impose trivial constraints because hard and soft sectors decouple—allowing the charges to affect only soft dynamics—this argument is shown to be flawed. This failure stems from a breakdown in infinite-dimensional symplectic geometry properties that hold in finite dimensions. Focusing on electromagnetism coupled to a massless charged scalar field in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, a perturbative classical calculation of the scattering map demonstrates that the sectors are inherently coupled. Although uncoupled at low orders, they become coupled at quartic order through the electromagnetic memory effect. This coupling persists regardless of how the hard and soft sectors are defined, including classical dressing of hard degrees of freedom. Consequently, conserved charges impose nontrivial constraints on hard degrees of freedom, a conclusion expected to extend to gravitational scattering and black hole formation or evaporation. Furthermore, in developing classical scattering theory, it is shown that generic Lorenz gauge solutions violate Strominger's proposed matching condition for the vector potential at spatial infinity, though a remedy is suggested. Additionally, when soft degrees of freedom are included, nonlinearities in the scattering map first appear at second order in Lorenz gauge, whereas they may emerge at third order in other gauges.

We define the concept of a factorized ramified structure for generic ramified irregular singular connections on a smooth projective curve. Leveraging the deformation theory associated with these structures, we establish a canonical $2$-form on the moduli space of such connections. Because the factorized ramified structure induces a duality on the moduli space's tangent space, this $2$-form is shown to be nondegenerate. Furthermore, by constructing an unfolding of the moduli space, we demonstrate that the $2$-form is $d$-closed. Utilizing Stokes data, we introduce the notion of local generalized isomonodromic deformation for generic unramified irregular singular connections on a unit disk. Through the lens of Jimbo-Miwa-Ueno theory applied to these unramified connections, this local deformation corresponds to the extendability of the connection family into an integrable connection; an analogous result holds for ramified connections. Grounded in this Jimbo-Miwa-Ueno framework, we construct a global generalized isomonodromic deformation on the moduli space of generic ramified connections by building a horizontal lift of a universal family of connections. Consequently, this global deformation allows the relative symplectic form on the moduli space to be lifted to a total closed form, designated as the generalized isomonodromic $2$-form.

We provide an explicit characterization of the terminal value $W$ for additive martingales within a notable branching stable process. Our analysis demonstrates that the right tail of $W$'s distribution exhibits exponential decay, whereas the left tail satisfies $-\log \mathbb{P}(W<x) \sim \frac{1}{2} (\log x)^2$ as $x \rightarrow 0+$. These findings stand in stark contrast to established results by Liu (2000, 2001) and Buraczewski (2009). Additionally, we establish that the law of $W$ is self-decomposable, implying a unimodal density, and we detail the asymptotic behavior of this density at both $0$ and $+\infty$.

The Cotton tensor is demonstrated to capture gravitational effects extending beyond general relativity. Any solution to the Einstein equations, whether including or excluding a cosmological constant, adheres to the field equations defined by the Cotton tensor, indicating that the cosmological constant functions as an integration constant. In this theoretical framework, a vacuum state is characterized by the vanishing of the Cotton tensor instead of the Ricci tensor. Furthermore, an exact Schwarzschild-like solution for a static, spherically symmetric source has been identified. Despite the field equations originally involving third-order derivatives, a variational principle reveals that they simplify into second-order differential equations.

The P{\O}D subdetector within the T2K near detector was used to measure the single $\pi^0$ production rate in neutral current neutrino interactions with water, utilizing a beam with a peak neutrino energy of 0.6 GeV. Data were collected during two distinct periods: one where the P{\O}D contained water ($2.64\times{}10^{20}$ protons-on-target) and another where it did not ($3.49 \times 10^{20}$ protons-on-target). The rate of neutral current single $\pi^0$ production on water was determined by subtracting the "water out" rate from the "water in" rate. This subtraction analysis resulted in 106 $\pm$ 41 (stat.) $\pm$ 69 (sys.) signal events, a result consistent with the nominal simulation prediction of 157 events. The measured-to-expected ratio is 0.68 $\pm$ 0.26 (stat.) $\pm$ 0.44 (sys.) $\pm$ 0.12 (flux). The nominal simulation employed a flux-integrated cross section of $7.63\times{}10^{-39}$ cm${}^2$ per nucleon, corresponding to an average neutrino interaction energy of 1.3 GeV.

The high-redshift galaxy cluster SRGe CL2305.2$-$2248 (also known as SPT-CL J2305$-$2248 or ACT-CL J2305.1$-$2248) is among the most massive structures at $z \simeq 0.76$, making it a significant subject for cosmological research. To optically identify the cluster, deep imaging was conducted using the 1.5-m Russian-Turkish telescope (RTT-150), complemented by Hubble Space Telescope archival data. This analysis enabled the detection of candidates for gravitationally lensed distant blue galaxies, appearing as arcs and arclets. A prominent giant arc located near the brightest cluster galaxies allowed researchers to determine the Einstein ring radius at $9.8 \pm 1.3$ arcseconds. Combined with the photometric redshift of the lensed source ($z_s = 2.44 \pm 0.07$), this measurement facilitated an independent mass estimation for the cluster. By extrapolating strong lensing findings to larger radii and applying density distribution models typical of relaxed clusters, the derived mass is approximately $1.5$ to $3$ times lower than values obtained from X-ray and microwave observations. This discrepancy is likely attributed to cluster merging, a phenomenon supported by the optical morphology of SRGe CL2305.2-2248.

Utilizing fundamental $\alpha$-attractor potentials, we examine an inflationary scenario within the high-$k$ limit. In this regime, cosmological perturbations are amplified significantly, leading to a breakdown characterized by an enhanced scalar power spectrum and substantial negative values for the Bardeen potential. This deep sub-horizon environment proves conducive to primordial black hole (PBH) formation. Working in the spatially flat gauge with $\delta\phi\neq 0$, we explicitly demonstrate how perturbations in both the inflaton field and the background gravitational field drive these enhancements and subsequent PBH generation. We compute the parameters $\sigma(M)$, $\beta(M)$, and $f_\mathrm{PBH}(M)$ near peaks in the density contrast profile to estimate the current dark matter fraction attributable to PBHs across specific mass scales. Our analysis indicates PBH formation within the wavenumber range $0.43\times 10^{13}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ to $9.8\times 10^{13}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, corresponding to masses between $1.35\times 10^{-13}M_\odot$ and $2.60\times 10^{-16}M_\odot$. These objects exhibit evaporation times ranging from $7.74\times 10^{33}$ sec down to $5.53\times 10^{25}$ sec, Hawking temperatures between $3.72\times 10^{-8}$ GeV and $1.93\times 10^{-5}$ GeV, and PBH fractions $f_\mathrm{PBH}(M)$ spanning approximately $6.12\times 10^{-6}$ to $3.63\times 10^{-1}$. The derived mass spectrum aligns with forecasts from LISA, WD, NS, DECIGO/AI, FL, and SIGWs, with the calculated $f_\mathrm{PBH}(M)$ values specifically overlapping with predictions from DECIGO/AI, FL, and SIGWs.

The fission barrier, a key parameter in quantitatively estimating various nuclear fission observables, is examined through the lens of deformation-based nuclear theory and its associated energy landscape. We detail the macroscopic-microscopic method for calculating these landscapes, noting that it is computationally simpler than the self-consistent mean-field approach and, due to its two-component structure, is more readily adaptable to experimental data. Additionally, we outline specific models and techniques employed to identify fission saddles. To illustrate these concepts, we present findings on fission barriers in actinides and superheavy nuclei derived from a single macroscopic-microscopic model. Finally, we compare these results with those obtained from other models, including various mean-field types.

This paper investigates $*$-conformal $\eta$-Ricci solitons within the context of Kenmotsu manifolds. We demonstrate that a Kenmotsu metric acting as a $*$-conformal $\eta$-Ricci soliton becomes an Einstein metric when the soliton vector field is contact. Additionally, we characterize the nature of the potential vector field and the manifold itself under the condition of being a gradient almost $*$-conformal $\eta$-Ricci soliton. Furthermore, we examine $*$-conformal $\eta$-Ricci solitons on $(\kappa,\mu)^\prime$-almost Kenmotsu manifolds, proving that such manifolds are Ricci flat and locally isometric to $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}(-4)\times\mathbb{R}^n$. Finally, we provide specific examples illustrating the existence of these solitons on Kenmotsu manifolds and $(\kappa,\mu)^\prime$-almost Kenmotsu manifolds.

A systematic comparison evaluates pairing properties of finite systems at nonzero temperatures across three principal statistical ensembles using exact solutions, alongside unprojected (FTBCS1+SCQRPA) and Lipkin-Nogami projected (FTLN1+SCQRPA) theories. These latter theories incorporate quasiparticle number fluctuations and coupling to pair vibrations within the self-consistent quasiparticle random-phase approximation. Numerical results were computed for the pairing gap, total energy, heat capacity, entropy, and microcanonical temperature using a doubly-folded equidistant multilevel pairing model. The FTLN1+SCQRPA approach yields predictions that align most closely with exact grand-canonical outcomes. Overall, all methods demonstrate that the superfluid-normal phase transition is significantly smoothed in finite systems. Additionally, a new formula is proposed for determining the empirical pairing gap with reasonable agreement to exact canonical results.

Since deep neural networks became the leading image classifiers a decade ago, there has been a noticeable shift away from max pooling, which selects the largest value among neighboring pixels. Given that max pooling was central to earlier classifier generations, we investigate this trend and its justification. We propose a theoretical framework examining ReLU-based approximations of max pooling and demonstrate that max pooling cannot be efficiently replicated using ReLU activations. Our analysis of optimal approximation errors reveals that while the error can be reduced to exponentially small levels relative to kernel size, achieving this demands an approximation of exponential complexity. Our findings provide a theoretical explanation for the declining use of max pooling in modern architectures. We conclude that the primary discrepancy between max pooling and optimal approximations—the significant gap between the maximum value and others within a pool—can be mitigated through alternative architectural choices or may simply not be prevalent in natural images.

Addressing the critical challenge of decentralized learning with private data, we introduce a new distillation-based method enabling multiple agents with non-iid private datasets to collaborate without exchanging data, model weights, or updates. This communication-efficient strategy leverages an unlabeled public dataset and employs multiple auxiliary heads per client, significantly boosting training efficiency amidst heterogeneous data distributions. Consequently, individual models maintain and enhance performance on their private tasks while substantially improving results on the global data distribution. We analyze the impacts of data and architectural heterogeneity, as well as communication graph topology, demonstrating that our agents achieve significantly better outcomes than learning in isolation.

Using dynamical mean-field theory, we demonstrate that the experimental signatures of nematic order in iron-based superconductors are fundamentally linked to electronic correlations within the Hund's correlated metallic state and cannot be described by a renormalized quasiparticle framework. Specifically, our findings indicate that: (i) in metals where correlations are dominated by Hund's coupling, nematic ordering does not cause a rigid energy shift in photoemission spectra but instead produces a more complex redistribution of spectral weight that aligns with experimental observations; (ii) this nematic ordering is defined by orbital-selective coherence driven by Hund's physics, consistent with the experimental picture.

Achieving an efficient balance between coverage and capacity in cellular networks requires precise control of antenna tilts. This paper introduces algorithms capable of learning optimal tilt control strategies, either by analyzing existing passive data or by generating data through active experimentation. We frame the development of these algorithms as a Best Policy Identification (BPI) challenge within the Contextual Linear Multi-Arm Bandits (CL-MAB) framework. In this model, each arm signifies a potential antenna tilt adjustment, the context reflects current network states, the reward measures performance gains that combine coverage and capacity, and the goal is to determine, with specified confidence, a near-optimal policy that maps contexts to the most rewarding actions. For both active and passive CL-MAB scenarios, we establish information-theoretic lower bounds on the sample complexity required to identify such policies and present algorithms that meet these theoretical limits. When applied to Remote Electrical Tilt (RET) optimization, our methods demonstrate the ability to derive optimal tilt update policies using significantly fewer data samples compared to naive or traditional rule-based approaches.

Although recent conditional image synthesis methods generate high-quality images, accurately controlling object positions and orientations remains difficult, often resulting in geometrically inconsistent outputs. To address this and enhance 3D geometric controllability, we introduce a novel approach for creating realistic images based on a configurable 3D scene layout. Our method accepts a 3D scene annotated with semantic class labels as input and trains a 3D scene painting network to generate color values for that scene. Using this trained network, we can render and manipulate realistic images of the input 3D scene. Since direct 3D color supervision is unavailable during training, we leverage an existing 2D semantic image synthesis technique. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach produces images with geometrically accurate structures and enables geometric manipulations, including changes in viewpoint and object poses, as well as adjustments to the painting style.

This research examines a variant of ordered trees in which rightmost edges, provided they do not terminate at an endnode, may be marked or unmarked. Originally proposed by E. Deutsch et al. to represent skew Dyck paths, these marked ordered trees serve as the subject of our study regarding the count of their deepest nodes. We derive explicit generating functions and determine that the average number of deepest nodes converges to $\frac{5}{3}$ as the tree size increases. This result contrasts with standard ordered trees, where the corresponding average approaches $2$.

Quantum gravitational phenomena may manifest at low energies if the metric field's wavefunction does not concentrate around a classical state. To investigate these departures from classicality within canonical quantum gravity, we introduce a "fluid of observers" into the low-energy framework and define a distance operator measured "at equal time" between them. Our results indicate that despite significant fluctuations in the metric field, a locally flat limit is restored in the vicinity of any given observer; thus, deviations from classicality do not have immediate local consequences. However, over larger separations, the expectation value of the distance operator diverges from standard Riemannian distance. Specifically, it becomes non-additive and cannot be derived by integrating a differential line element. This resulting "beyond Riemannian" geometry resembles a metric space akin to embedded Riemannian manifolds where distances are measured as chords through the ambient space. By examining triangles in the limit of vanishing size, we analyze deviations from flat space. These beyond-Riemannian deviations relative to flat space are of the same magnitude as standard Riemannian ones but exhibit qualitative differences. Finally, we briefly explore potential links to holography and the black hole information paradox.

This research investigates the volumes of extrinsic balls and the capacities of extrinsic annuli within minimal submanifolds that are properly immersed with controlled radial sectional curvatures into an ambient manifold possessing a pole. The primary findings focus on comparing these volumes and capacities against those of a rotationally symmetric model manifold. Leveraging the asymptotic behavior of these geometric quantities, we derive upper bounds for the number of ends and provide estimates for the fundamental tone of the submanifolds under consideration.

The global COVID-19 pandemic has caused profound devastation, resulting in significant loss of life, economic downturns, travel bans, trade deficits, and a collapsing economy that impacts real estate, employment, health benefits, access to care, and overall quality of life. Relying solely on anticipated vaccines will not be sufficient to overcome the pandemic and restore normalcy. Instead, effective public health intervention requires four core pillars: diagnostic testing for both symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals, contact tracing, quarantine for those infected or exposed, and strict hygiene adherence at individual and community levels. Currently, digital technologies such as mobile applications, web dashboards, and online self-assessment tools are being utilized for testing. This discussion examines various digital solutions adopted by universities, businesses, and other organizations, summarizing the challenges they face regarding information quality, privacy, and user-centric issues. Although numerous digital solutions exist and are under development, they often differ in the quantity and quality of shared information, which can overwhelm users. Viewing the testing landscape through a digital lens reveals multiple hurdles, including data privacy concerns, costs, and miscommunication. Digitalization is destined to guide COVID-19 testing efforts, with blockchain-based systems offering potential for privacy preservation and ensuring data ownership remains with the user. Additionally, digital health passports containing accurate and relevant information present another viable solution. In this preliminary draft, we outline existing challenges and propose corresponding solutions.

The connection between determinantal point processes (DPPs) and free fermionic frameworks is established; however, we highlight that within the context of free fermionic algebras, Pfaffian point processes (PfPPs) arise naturally. We demonstrate that a positive contraction on a "doubled" one-particle space, equipped with specific additional structure, uniquely generates a PfPP. Building on Olshanski's reversal of the standard free fermion-to-DPP mapping, which involves constructing fermionic states from quasi-invariant probability measures and defining measure "perfectness," we introduce a verification method for perfectness. We prove that Schur measures satisfy this condition whenever they are quasi-invariant under the symmetric group's action. Furthermore, we examine conditional measures for PfPPs linked to projection operators, ultimately showing that these conditional measures remain PfPPs corresponding to projections onto explicitly defined subspaces.

Although long-term indoor environmental quality affects employee productivity, its short-term impact at the meeting level remains uncertain. This study investigates the link between a meeting room's sensory pleasantness and meeting productivity. Through a 28-item survey of 363 online participants, we identified three core dimensions of the meeting experience: productivity, psychological safety, and room pleasantness. To quantify room pleasantness, we created ComFeel, an unobtrusive indoor environmental sensing system utilizing miniaturized "Gecko" devices to monitor light, temperature, and gas levels. Data was gathered across 29 real-world meetings, totaling 1,373 minutes of sensor readings, alongside self-reported assessments of productivity, safety, and room pleasantness from participants. Consistent with expectations, results showed that for every standard deviation increase in psychological safety, the likelihood of a meeting being productive rose by 35%. Crucially, room pleasantness also significantly boosted productivity probability by up to 25% per unit increase, validating the substantial short-term influence of the indoor environment on meeting outcomes.

Let $p$ be a fixed prime and $q$ a power of $p$. For any curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$ equipped with a local system, the traces of Frobenius at closed points generate a number field called the trace field. We demonstrate that for pointed curves of type $(g,n)$ in characteristic $p$, when considering rank two local systems subject to a condition at infinity, the collection of trace fields that are unramified at $p$ and have bounded degree is finite. This finding validates observations made by Kontsevich through numerical experiments, which relate closely to the function field analogue of Maeda's conjecture. Furthermore, we establish a comparable finiteness theorem across all primes $p$. A central component of our proofs involves the boundedness of abelian schemes of $\mathrm{GL}_2$-type over curves in positive characteristic, which serves as an analogue of Faltings' Arakelov theorem for abelian varieties within this context.

By applying soliton theory within a nonlinear elastic medium, we forecast a new phenomenon termed a "phononic tsunami," defined by a significant surge in the local amplitude of phonon modes. To facilitate experimental observation, we suggest utilizing a wedge-shaped sample where a sharp edge mimics the shoaling effect, allowing for the detection of this localized amplification. In conjunction with the eigenfrequencies of both transverse and longitudinal phonon modes, we derive characteristic dispersion relations that serve as definitive signatures of a phononic tsunami. Our predictions are supported by analytical calculations and numerical simulations demonstrating the feasibility of realizing this nonlinear effect in the proposed geometry. Ultimately, our findings establish a framework for designing novel experiments to generate and study phononic tsunamis in appropriate materials.

This study establishes three sets of non-perturbative fragmentation functions, complete with uncertainties, for $B$-hadrons, $J/\psi$ mesons, and muons produced via semileptonic $B$ decays. Each set achieves next-to-next-to leading order (NNLO) accuracy and incorporates next-to-next-to leading logarithmic soft gluon resummation. A distinctive aspect of these new functions is their full consistency with our NNLO formalism for final states containing identified $B$, $J/\psi$, or $\mu$ particles. Utilizing these fragmentation functions, we generate state-of-the-art predictions for such final states within $t\bar t$ events at the LHC, with particular focus on observables probing the top quark mass. This work paves the way for numerous LHC applications, including open $B$ production and $B$ production in association with bosons.

Model-based reinforcement learning offers a highly effective strategy for practical robotics, primarily due to its superior data efficiency compared to model-free approaches. However, existing state-of-the-art methods depend on shaped reward signals, which are often challenging to design and implement. To address this limitation, we introduce a streamlined model-based technique specifically designed for sparse-reward multi-goal scenarios, eliminating the necessity for complex reward engineering. Named Imaginary Hindsight Experience Replay, this method reduces real-world interactions by integrating imaginary data into policy updates. To enhance exploration within sparse-reward environments, the policy is trained using standard Hindsight Experience Replay augmented with curiosity-driven intrinsic rewards. Evaluation on the OpenAI Gym Fetch Robotics benchmarks demonstrates that this approach achieves an order-of-magnitude improvement in data efficiency on average compared to the leading model-free methods.

We investigate how a network of coupled, identical agents responds to perturbations within the thermodynamic limit, where the agents undergo stochastic evolution typically representing non-equilibrium states. The system is biased toward a shared center of mass. Using mean-field Fokker-Planck equations, we establish Kramers-Kronig relations and sum rules for linear susceptibilities, subsequently proposing corrections for the macroscopic regime that self-consistently account for mutual interactions between systems. These interactions generate a memory effect. Furthermore, we derive conditions under which phase transitions arise specifically from system-to-system coupling. These transitions, occurring in the thermodynamic limit, are characterized by the divergence of linear response without a corresponding divergence in the integrated autocorrelation time for a specific observable. We distinguish these endogenous phase transitions from other linear response pathologies associated with critical transitions. Finally, we demonstrate how our findings clarify the characteristics of the Desai-Zwanzig model and the Bonilla-Casado-Morillo model, which exemplify paradigmatic equilibrium and non-equilibrium phase transitions, respectively.

Lead bias is a prevalent issue in news articles that often overshadows the learning signals for neural extractive summarizers, significantly hindering their performance on data lacking or possessing different biases. This paper presents a new method to reduce this lead bias, directing the summarizer's attention more toward content semantics. Experiments conducted on two news corpora with varying levels of lead bias demonstrate that our approach effectively diminishes the model's learned bias and enhances its generalization to out-of-distribution data, with minimal to no degradation in performance on in-distribution data.

This work investigates supersymmetric open strings within the type IIB $AdS_3 \times S^3 \times S^3 \times S^1$ background, which includes mixed R-R and NS-NS fluxes. The analysis centers on strings terminating on a straight line at the $AdS_3$ boundary, interpreted as line operators in the corresponding dual two-dimensional CFT. We examine both classical solutions and their quadratic fluctuations. It is demonstrated that strings fixed at a single point in $S^3 \times S^3 \times S^1$ (obeying Dirichlet conditions) preserve 1/2 of the supersymmetry (1/2 BPS). Furthermore, we identify that strings anchored at various locations on specific submanifolds of $S^3 \times S^3 \times S^1$ retain partial supersymmetry, enabling the construction of supersymmetric smeared states via superposition; these states span a range from 1/2 BPS down to 1/8 BPS. Beyond smeared configurations, we also find 1/4 BPS and 1/8 BPS solutions satisfying Neumann boundary conditions. These diverse supersymmetric string states are linked through a network of interpolating BPS boundary conditions.
