By utilizing half-plane representations, the scattering problem is reformulated as a coupled system consisting of (1) a localized finite element discretization near the scatterer and (2) integral equations where the unknowns are the traces of the solution on the boundaries of a finite set of overlapping half-planes within the domain. Although satisfactory numerical results have been achieved for real wavenumbers, the well-posedness and equivalence of the HSM formulation to the original scattering problem have previously been proven only for complex wavenumbers. In this paper, we demonstrate that, for a homogeneous background, the HSM formulation is also equivalent to the original scattering problem for real wavenumbers and thus well-posed, assuming the traces satisfy radiation conditions at infinity analogous to the standard Sommerfeld radiation condition. A pivotal element of our proof establishes that if the trace on a half-plane boundary meets this new radiation condition, the corresponding solution to the half-plane Dirichlet problem satisfies the Sommerfeld radiation condition in a slightly smaller half-plane. We anticipate that this final result will hold independent interest, particularly in the study of rough surface scattering.

The existence of quantum spin liquid states as the natural ground state of the Kitaev model has driven the search for new materials exhibiting Kitaev physics, yet such candidates remain scarce. By combining $ab$ initio calculations with model Hamiltonian approaches, we suggest that the Ruddlesden-Popper compound Sr$_4$RhO$_6$ fits within this category. Employing a tight-binding model and exact diagonalization, we demonstrate that despite significant trigonal-like distortion, the electronic and magnetic characteristics of Sr$_4$RhO$_6$ are accurately described using pseudo-spin = 1/2 states. Magnetic interactions between these pseudo-spins, calculated via second-order perturbation theory, exhibit strong bond-dependent anisotropy, notably featuring antiferromagnetic Kitaev and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions. Furthermore, the gapped spin-wave spectra derived from linear spin-wave theory align with the material's inherent magnetic frustration. Detailed analysis indicates that the spin-wave behavior results from a combination of highly anisotropic interactions, implying that a simpler minimal model is insufficient to capture the current case. Ultimately, the key insights gained regarding the coupling between local structural features and magnetic properties in Sr$_4$RhO$_6$ are expected to benefit future research in this domain.

The Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerant (PBFT) consensus mechanism stands as a foundational algorithm in blockchain technology; consequently, evaluating its performance is a complex and intriguing challenge due to the intricate nature of its consensus operations within peer-to-peer networks. This paper introduces a streamlined stochastic performance model for PBFT, characterizing it not merely as a queueing system with complex service durations but also as a level-independent quasi-birth-and-death (QBD) process. Leveraging the matrix-geometric solution derived from this QBD process, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the stability of the PBFT consensus system and enable the numerical calculation of the stationary probability vector. Furthermore, we derive four key performance metrics for the PBFT mechanism, which can be computed numerically. Through numerical examples, we validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate how these four metrics are affected by critical PBFT parameters. Ultimately, utilizing the theory of multi-dimensional Markov processes, we suggest that the methodology and results presented herein are broadly applicable to extensive research on PBFT consensus and potentially other consensus mechanisms.

This study reports the initial findings from an ongoing effort to conduct simultaneous multiwavelength observations of flares on nearby active M dwarfs. We monitored the nearby dM3.5e star EV Lac using five observatories: NASA's TESS, NASA's Swift Observatory, NASA's NICER, the University of Hawaii 2.2-m telescope (UH88), and the Las Cumbres Observatory Global Telescope (LCOGT) Network. Over approximately 25 days of TESS monitoring, we collected three simultaneous UV/X-ray datasets from Swift totaling ~18 ks, 21 simultaneous epochs of NICER X-ray data summing to ~98 ks, a ~3-hour observation with UH88, and a ~3-hour observation with LCOGT. We detected 56 flares in the TESS light curve with estimated energies ranging from log $E_{\rm T}$ (erg) = 30.5 to 33.2, nine flares in the Swift UVM2 light curve with energies between log $E_{\rm UV}$ (erg) = 29.3 and 31.1, 14 flares in the NICER light curve with minimum energies spanning log $E_{\rm N}$ (erg) = 30.5 to 32.3, and one flare in the LCOGT light curve with log $E_{\rm L}$ (erg) = 31.6. Our analysis reveals that the flare frequency distributions (FFDs) for TESS and NICER flares exhibit comparable slopes ($\beta_{\rm T}$ = -0.67$\pm$0.09 and $\beta_{\rm N}$ = -0.65$\pm$0.19), whereas the FFD for UVOT flares displays a shallower slope ($\beta_{\rm U}$ = -0.38$\pm$0.13). Additionally, we found no conclusive evidence supporting either the first ionization potential (FIP) or the inverse FIP effect during coronal flares on EV Lac.

Charged Lepton Flavor Violation is anticipated to be a primary instrument for uncovering physics beyond the Standard Model. The COMET experiment is designed to detect the neutrinoless coherent conversion of a muon into an electron within the field of a nucleus. Since this process has never been observed, its discovery would constitute definitive proof of new physics. The experimental sensitivity, defined as the ratio of the muon-to-electron conversion rate to the total muon capture rate, is projected to improve by a factor of 100 to 10,000 over the next decade. COMET will operate at J-PARC, achieving single-event sensitivities on the order of $10^{-15}$ and $10^{-17}$ in Phase-I and Phase-II, respectively. This ambitious objective is accomplished by implementing a high-quality pulsed beam and an exceptionally powerful muon source, coupled with a detector system capable of withstanding a harsh radiation environment. Construction of the new beam line, superconducting magnets, detectors, and electronics is currently underway for the upcoming Phase-I experiment. This presentation outlines the experimental methods, sensitivities, and backgrounds, alongside the current status and future prospects.

While most reactive system synthesis methods analyze scenarios as two-player games with full observation, many real-world applications involve environments composed of multiple distinct entities requiring active communication for information gathering. This paper models such settings as a team of players, explicitly tracking the information state of each individual. This approach enables the synthesis of programs capable of interacting with distributed environments and utilizing multiple interacting information sources. The corresponding synthesis problem is equivalent to solving a specific class of Petri games—multi-player games on Petri nets where the system is represented by a distinguished token and the environment by an arbitrary number of tokens. Although the general decidability of Petri games remains unresolved, we demonstrate that synthesis in these distributed environments is solvable in polynomial time when the environment consists of at most two tokens. Conversely, the problem is NP-complete for any fixed number of three or more environment tokens, and EXPTIME-complete if the number of environment tokens scales with the size of the net.

Tracing out environmental degrees of freedom is an essential step for simulating open quantum systems, yet it constitutes an information loss that complicates the understanding of dynamics when system-environment interactions are strong. Such isolated dynamics lack a time-local description, exhibiting non-Markovian behavior where memory effects create complex, hard-to-interpret features. To overcome this, we demonstrate a method to infer any correlation function of a Gaussian environment using system correlations—calculated via any approach—provided the system-environment coupling is linear. This technique not only enables the reconstruction of the full dynamics for both system and environment but also facilitates the study of how a system influences its surroundings. To ensure accurate bath dynamics, we employ a numerically exact simulation strategy based on constructing and contracting a tensor network that represents the process tensor of the open quantum system, allowing for the exact determination of any system correlation function. As a demonstration of this method's utility, we illustrate how heat transfers between different modes of a bosonic bath when coupled to a two-level system driven off-resonantly.

Region-based type systems serve as effective instruments for diverse program analyses. We present a novel inference algorithm for region types grounded in the concept of abstract environment transformation. This approach examines a method's code just once, regardless of how many times the method is invoked with varying region types across the program. The components of this abstract transformation function as equality and subtyping constraints that encapsulate the program's flow data. Specifically, we utilize access graphs within the definition of these transformations to ensure the algorithm's termination, as they offer a finite depiction of field access paths.

This research examines the online clustering problem, where data points arrive sequentially. The algorithm organizes these points into similarity groups. As each new item $v$ arrives, its similarity relationships with all previously seen items $u$ are revealed, indicating whether $v$ is similar to $u$. The algorithm has the capability to assign $v$ to a new cluster or merge existing clusters. When the goal is to minimize disagreements between the clustering and the input data, we demonstrate that a straightforward greedy approach achieves an $O(n)$-competitive ratio, which is proven to be optimal. Conversely, when the objective is to maximize agreements, the greedy algorithm attains a 0.5-competitive ratio; we further establish that no online algorithm can exceed a 0.834-competitive ratio. Finally, we show that performance better than 1/2 is achievable by presenting a randomized algorithm with a competitive ratio of $0.5 + c$, where $c$ is a small positive constant.

We present a novel audio source separation framework utilizing embeddings within a hyperbolic manifold to efficiently capture the hierarchical connections between time-frequency features and sound sources. Drawing on recent advancements in applying hyperbolic embeddings to hierarchical data in text and imagery, our approach generates a hyperbolic representation for every time-frequency bin of a mixed signal and derives separation masks via hyperbolic softmax layers. Evaluated on a synthetic dataset comprising mixtures of human speech and musical instruments, our model achieved source-to-distortion ratios comparable to a Euclidean baseline, while demonstrating superior performance at lower embedding dimensions. Additionally, we observe that time-frequency regions with multiple overlapping sources are mapped toward the center of the hyperbolic space—the area of highest uncertainty—and leverage this certainty metric to effectively balance artifact suppression against interference reduction during the isolation of individual sounds.

Achieving locomotion toward arbitrary targets on physical hardware continues to pose significant challenges for reinforcement learning. This paper introduces a hierarchical learning framework designed to enhance both the sample efficiency and generalizability of locomotion skills on real-world robots. Our method decomposes goal-oriented movement into two distinct tasks: acquiring diverse primitive skills and employing model-based planning to sequence them. By parameterizing these primitives as cyclic movements, we improve learning efficiency on a 18-degree-of-freedom robot. Furthermore, we develop coarse dynamics models for these primitive cycles and integrate them into a model predictive control system. This approach enables the robot to walk to arbitrary destinations up to 12 meters away, achieving this in approximately two hours of training from scratch on hardware. Experiments conducted on a Daisy hexapod in both simulation and physical environments confirm the method's effectiveness in reaching distant targets across varied settings and despite sensory noise.

This study introduces a stochastic synchronous cellular automaton modeled on a square grid, where the rules derive from the SEIR (susceptible, exposed, infected, recovered) framework. The probabilistic parameters are grounded in real-world data regarding human mortality and SARS-CoV-2 characteristics. Computer simulations demonstrate how neighborhood radius affects the count of infected and deceased agents within the artificial population. Expanding the neighborhood radius accelerates epidemic spread. Furthermore, across a broad spectrum of interactions involving exposed agents (asymptomatic and undiagnosed), isolating infected individuals fails to halt disease propagation. These findings underscore aggressive testing as a critical strategy for mitigating large infection peaks in diseases resembling SARS-CoV-2.

Most microrobots are built from compliant materials that resist analytical modeling, thereby restricting the effectiveness of conventional model-based controllers. Furthermore, difficulties in gathering data on these micro-robots, combined with significant discrepancies between simulations and physical reality, hinder the application of current model-based learning and sim-to-real transfer approaches. To address this, we introduce a novel framework called Residual Model Learning (RML), which utilizes approximate models to significantly lower the sample complexity required for accurate robot modeling. Our results demonstrate that RML enables the creation of a model for the Harvard Ambulatory MicroRobot (HAMR) using only 12 seconds of passively collected interaction data. This learned model serves as an effective "proxy-simulator," facilitating the acquisition of walking and turning behaviors through model-free reinforcement learning. RML offers a general solution for learning from minimal interaction data, and our experiments with HAMR clearly show that it substantially outperforms existing methods.

This study establishes precise late-time asymptotic behaviors for solutions to the wave equation with angular frequencies $\ell$ or higher within the domain of outer communications and up to the event horizon of subextremal Reissner-Nordstr\"om spacetimes. The derived asymptotics provide sharp upper and lower decay rates that align with Price's law on these backgrounds. We develop a framework for inverting the time operator, resulting in an explicit formula for the leading-order asymptotic coefficient expressed via Newman-Penrose charges at null infinity related to time integrals. Our approach relies exclusively on physical space methods. For every angular frequency $\ell$, we demonstrate a sharp hierarchy of $r$-weighted radially commuted estimates extending to a length of $2\ell+5$, which is supplemented by a new hierarchy of weighted elliptic estimates with a length of $\ell+1$.

Stereo reconstruction models trained on small images fail to generalize to high-resolution data, and training on high-resolution inputs is often impractical due to data scarcity and computational constraints. This paper introduces Occlusion-aware Recurrent binocular Stereo matching (ORStereo), a solution that trains exclusively on low-disparity stereo images. By framing the task as residual updates and refinements of an initial prediction, ORStereo successfully generalizes to unseen high-resolution images with large disparity ranges. Although trained on images with a disparity range limited to 256 pixels, the model can process 4K-resolution inputs containing over 1000 disparities within limited GPU memory. Evaluated on both synthetic and real-world high-resolution datasets, ORStereo achieves performance on 4K images comparable to state-of-the-art methods trained on large disparity ranges. Furthermore, compared to other approaches trained solely on low-resolution images, ORStereo demonstrates a 70% accuracy improvement on 4K-resolution data.

This study reports the first observations of a square lattice structure within a monodisperse complex plasma system, addressing a long-standing experimental challenge. Experiments were performed using the tabletop L-shaped Dusty Plasma Experimental (DPEx-II) device under a DC glow discharge Argon plasma. By precisely regulating the vertical potential confining the charged particles and the strength of ion wake charge interactions with the dust, we guided the system into a crystalline phase characterized by a square lattice. This transition happens when the vertical confinement strength drops slightly below a critical threshold, causing the monodisperse hexagonal 2D dust crystal to buckle and form a narrowly separated bilayer state (a quasi-2D configuration). Additionally, Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations conducted with parameters matching our experiment offer theoretical insights into this transition process.

Latent variable models serve as potent statistical instruments capable of revealing meaningful differences among patients or cells by deducing unobserved hidden states from high-dimensional observable data. However, a primary limitation of existing approaches is their failure to generate sparse and interpretable latent representations. Furthermore, incorporating prior knowledge about the data's latent structure remains statistically difficult when such partial information is accessible. To overcome these challenges, we introduce spex-LVM, a factorial latent variable model employing sparse priors to facilitate the discovery of explainable factors informed by domain-specific data. By leveraging established biomedical pathway knowledge, spex-LVM automatically maps annotated attributes to latent factors, producing results that are interpretable and aligned with the specific domain of interest. Assessments on both simulated and real single-cell RNA-seq datasets confirm that the model robustly detects relevant structures in a transparent manner, effectively separating technical noise from genuine biomedical variation, and offers pathway annotations adapted to individual datasets. The implementation can be accessed at https://github.com/MLO-lab/spexlvm.

We introduce an attentive encoder that integrates tree-structured recursive neural networks with sequential recurrent neural networks to model sentence pairs. While current attentive models focus attention on sequential structures, we propose a method to embed attention within the tree topology. Specifically, for a pair of sentences, our encoder utilizes an RNN-generated representation of one sentence to direct the structural encoding of the other sentence along its dependency parse tree. We assess this proposed encoder across three tasks: semantic similarity, paraphrase identification, and true-false question selection. Experimental findings demonstrate that our encoder surpasses all baselines and achieves state-of-the-art performance on two of the tasks.

The exclusive occurrence of $\beta$-D-ribofuranose in nucleic acids remains a puzzle in prebiotic chemistry, especially since pyranose forms are thermodynamically more stable at equilibrium. However, precise data on the relative furanose-to-pyranose ratios at temperatures exceeding approximately 50$^{\,\rm o}$C are currently unavailable. In this study, we utilize a combination of NMR spectroscopy and statistical mechanics modeling to forecast a population reversal between furanose and pyranose at equilibrium under high-temperature conditions. Crucially, we demonstrate that a sustained temperature gradient can drive an open isomerization network toward a non-equilibrium steady state, thereby enhancing furanose abundance beyond equilibrium thermodynamic limits. Furthermore, we show that the non-equilibrium selection of furanose peaks at optimal dissipation, defined by the temperature gradient and isomerization energy barriers. The predicted optimal conditions align with temperature decreases observed in hydrothermal vents linked to recent lava flows on the ocean floor.

This study examines static, spherically symmetric configurations of stars composed of barotropic perfect fluids within two type-II minimally modified gravity frameworks: VCDM and VCCDM. These theories are characterized by the absence of extra degrees of freedom in the gravitational sector, propagating only two gravitational waves alongside matter fields, identical to General Relativity (GR). By enforcing physical boundary conditions on the Misner-Sharp mass, we determine that the solutions derived in V(C)CDM are precisely equivalent to those in GR, specifically satisfying the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equation.

Changing Look Active Galactic Nuclei (CLAGNs) exhibit intricate behaviors in their X-ray spectra and variations in line-of-sight column density, though the underlying physical mechanisms remain uncertain. This study investigates the spectral characteristics of the CLAGN NGC 1365 by analyzing combined XMM-Newton and NuSTAR data to clarify the nature of CL variability. Our modeling indicates that the mass accretion rate fluctuates between $0.003\pm 0.001$ and $0.009\pm0.002$ $\dot M_{\rm Edd}$, while the dynamic corona shifts from $28\pm 3$ to $10\pm1$ $r_g$. We observed a correlation between the variable absorption column density and both the mass accretion rate and coronal geometry. Furthermore, the derived wind velocities were found to be too low relative to the escape velocity to successfully drive winds from the disc during epochs of high column density, suggesting that the observed high and variable absorption results from failed disc winds. The estimated ratio of mass outflow to inflow rates in the inner disc region ranges from $0.019\pm0.006$ to $0.12\pm0.04$. Spectral fitting of the combined dataset yielded a constant central black hole mass of $4.38\pm0.34$ to $4.51\pm0.29 \times10^{6} M_\odot$, aligning with previous results. Additionally, confidence contours for $N_H$ relative to other parameters demonstrate that the fitted model parameters are robust and non-degenerate. Our findings conclude that the changing accretion rate—a fundamental physical quantity—and the coronal geometry are the drivers of CL phenomena in NGC 1365. The physical framework proposed in this work integrates both variable continuum and variable absorbing medium scenarios.

We investigate observational signatures of magnetic fields within simulations of a Milky-Way-like disc featuring supernova-driven turbulence and self-consistent chemistry. Specifically, we post-process two SILCC Project datasets initialized with magnetic field amplitudes of $B_0 = 3$ and $6 \, \mu$G to examine the evolution of Faraday rotation measures (RM) and synchrotron luminosity. To calculate RM, we evaluate three distinct electron density ($n_e$) models: a constant density, and two estimates derived from the density of ionized species and the fraction of total gas, respectively. Our findings reveal that RM profiles are highly sensitive to the chosen $n_e$ models, underscoring the critical need for accurate electron distribution data when probing magnetic fields via Faraday RMs. Additionally, we estimate synchrotron luminosity using a semi-analytical cosmic ray model and observe a temporal decrease linked to the dissipation of magnetic energy. Ratios of magnetic, cosmic ray, and thermal energy densities indicate that equipartition is not maintained in most interstellar medium regions. Notably, assuming equipartition between cosmic ray and magnetic energy could lead to misinterpretations of observed synchrotron emission.

We tackle a pivotal obstacle hindering the creation of Majorana-based topological qubits using semiconductor-superconductor hybrids: the precise quantification of disorder caused by accidental charge impurities in these devices. Since disorder profoundly impacts Majorana physics yet remains experimentally elusive in such hybrid systems, a rigorous theoretical framework is essential. To achieve this, we formulate a microscopic theory that (i) quantitatively models the effective potential from a charge impurity in a semiconductor wire proximitized by a superconductor by self-consistently solving the three-dimensional Schrödinger-Poisson equations; (ii) captures the low-energy physics of the hybrid system under s-wave superconductivity, spin-orbit coupling, Zeeman splitting, and multi-impurity disorder by applying the results from (i) within a standard free fermion framework; and (iii) connects these microscopic findings to experimental observables by producing tunneling differential conductance maps dependent on control parameters like the Zeeman field and chemical potential. Our analysis reveals that charge impurities create significant barriers to realizing and detecting Majorana zero modes, directly affecting qubit development. Crucially, our work offers a clear roadmap for future progress, specifying the required levels of material quality and semiconductor purity necessary to successfully construct a topological qubit.

Classification, recommendation, and ranking tasks frequently entail competing objectives subject to constraints like fairness or diversity. These optimization challenges are difficult due to non-convex functions and the need to balance user preferences. While Pareto solutions define the optimal frontier for jointly optimizing multiple conflicting goals, common linear-scalarization methods face significant hurdles: they may fail to converge to a global optimum and typically yield only a single solution per execution. Consequently, constructing a Pareto front—which comprises the global optima across various trade-offs—requires multiple runs that all successfully converge, making it computationally intractable for practical applications due to high overhead, poor scalability, and diminished accuracy. To address this, we introduce a robust, cost-effective, two-stage hybrid neural Pareto optimization framework that scales efficiently with data dimensions, functions, and constraints. The first stage utilizes a neural network to rapidly identify a weak Pareto front using Fritz-John conditions as a discriminator, without requiring convexity assumptions for objectives or constraints. The second stage applies an efficient Pareto filter to extract the strong Pareto optimal subset from the weak front generated in stage one. Furthermore, Fritz-John conditions establish theoretical bounds on the approximation error between the true front and the network-extracted weak front. Numerical experiments confirm the method's accuracy and efficiency across canonical benchmark problems and a fairness optimization task.

Maintaining cost-effective visual representation and rapid query-by-example search for web-scale retrieval on moderate hardware remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a fast, robust method that achieves both objectives, delivering state-of-the-art results for image-to-video search. We propose critical improvements to established indexing and visual representation techniques, optimizing for speed, accuracy, and moderate resource usage. Furthermore, we enhance the method's effectiveness on specific visual challenges by leveraging individual decisions from both local and global descriptors during query processing. Local descriptors are particularly effective for identifying copied or duplicated scenes with significant geometric deformations, such as changes in scale, orientation, or affine transformation, whereas global descriptors are better suited for near-duplicate and semantic searches. Experiments conducted on the large-scale Stanford I2V dataset demonstrate that the proposed method offers superior complexity and query processing efficiency for large-scale retrieval, even when combining local and global representations. The approach achieves state-of-the-art performance based on Mean Average Precision (MAP) scores. Additionally, we report updated MAP scores after refining ground annotations based on the retrieval results, confirming the method's actual high performance.

Recent advances in passive behavioral biometrics, such as analyzing gestures or footsteps, offer a promising alternative to traditional identification methods like face or fingerprint scanning, particularly in constrained scenarios. However, current sensing technologies often demand extensive data traces and fail to simultaneously identify multiple individuals. To address these limitations, we introduce \systemname, a passive multi-person identification framework that utilizes deep learning for footstep separation and recognition. Unlike existing gait-based systems that suffer from significant latency due to the need for prolonged data collection, \systemname\ can identify an individual based on as few as a single step, drastically reducing identification delay. Furthermore, to ensure adaptability to varying walking speeds, environmental changes, and unseen subjects, we employ adversarial learning to enhance domain generalization and accuracy. Additionally, the system leverages the richness of footstep data and spatial awareness to defend against replay attacks. We have implemented a prototype of \systemname\ using off-the-shelf hardware and evaluated it in standard indoor environments. Experimental results indicate a cross-domain identification accuracy exceeding 90%.

This work reviews the theoretical and experimental advancements in the Glauber model regarding multiple nucleon and/or parton scatterings over the past decade and a half, following operations with proton and nuclear beams at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and with light and heavy ion collisions at BNL's Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC). The summary covers the field's current state-of-the-art, including measurements of inclusive inelastic cross sections for protons and nuclei, improvements in modeling proton and nuclear density profiles and their fluctuations, the incorporation of subnucleonic degrees of freedom, experimental methods for determining collision centrality, validation of binary scaling for hard scattering cross sections, and constraints on quark-gluon matter transport properties derived from varying initial-state conditions in relativistic hydrodynamics. These developments affirm the validity and utility of the Glauber formalism for quantitatively analyzing QCD matter produced in high-energy collisions across systems ranging from protons to uranium nuclei of vastly different sizes.

**Objective.** Dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) offers significant potential for enhancing contrast, minimizing artifacts, and enabling material decomposition in advanced imaging. However, increasing the number of measurements typically raises the radiation dose. Consequently, reducing either the projection count per energy level or the X-ray source intensity is crucial, yet this creates a more ill-posed tomographic reconstruction problem.

**Approach.** We introduced the Multi-Channel Convolutional Analysis Operator Learning (MCAOL) method, which leverages shared spatial features across attenuation images at varying energies. Our proposed optimization framework jointly reconstructs low- and high-energy attenuation images using mixed-norm regularization applied to sparse features derived from pre-trained convolutional filters via the Convolutional Analysis Operator Learning (CAOL) algorithm.

**Main Results.** Comprehensive experiments utilizing both simulated and real CT data confirmed the efficacy of our methods, demonstrating superior reconstruction accuracy compared to CAOL and iterative approaches employing single or joint total-variation (TV) regularization.

**Significance.** Qualitative and quantitative analyses of sparse-view and low-dose DECT data indicate that the proposed MCAOL method surpasses both independent CAOL applications for each energy and various existing state-of-the-art model-based iterative reconstruction (MBIR) techniques, thereby facilitating significant radiation dose reduction.

The pumping lemma for context-free languages, which parallels the well-known lemma for regular languages, pertains to pushdown automata. While the regular language version relies on the pigeonhole principle applied to deterministic automata, the context-free version is typically established via an equivalence with context-free grammars and the more advanced Ogden's lemma. This paper offers a proof of the pumping lemma for context-free languages that is based on pushdown automata rather than context-free grammars.

Quantum LDPC codes offer a promising route toward low-overhead, fault-tolerant quantum computing. Nevertheless, the absence of geometric constraints in general LDPC codes often leads to naive implementations that connect distant qubits via crossing links, posing significant hardware fabrication challenges and potentially inducing performance-reducing crosstalk. To address this, we introduce a 2D layout strategy for quantum LDPC codes by breaking down their Tanner graphs into a limited set of non-crossing planar layers. Each layer accommodates long-range connections without intersection. For any CSS code featuring a degree-$\delta$ Tanner graph, we construct stabilizer measurement circuits with a depth no greater than $(2\delta +2)$ utilizing up to $\lceil \delta/2 \rceil$ layers. Experimental observations indicate a circuit-noise threshold of 0.28% for a positive-rate code family employing 49 physical qubits per logical qubit. At a physical error rate of $10^{-4}$, this family achieves a logical error rate of $10^{-15}$ while requiring fourteen times fewer physical qubits compared to the surface code.

A word is defined as square-free if it lacks any nonempty factor of the form $XX$. Thue's renowned 1906 theorem establishes that square-free words of arbitrary length can be formed using an alphabet of three letters. This study examines square-free words with specific properties regarding single-letter deletions and extensions. A square-free word is termed "steady" if it retains its square-free status after removing any single letter. We demonstrate the existence of infinitely many steady words over a four-letter alphabet and show that steady words of any desired length can be constructed by selecting letters from alphabets of size seven assigned to each position. We conjecture that the required alphabet size can be reduced to four, which is the theoretical minimum. Conversely, we investigate square-free words that remain square-free after inserting a single suitably chosen letter at every possible position, labeling them "bifurcate." Surprisingly, we prove that over any fixed alphabet of at least three letters, every steady word is also bifurcate. Furthermore, we explore families of bifurcate words with a natural tree structure, specifically proving the existence of an infinite tree of doubly infinite bifurcate words over an alphabet of size twelve.

This paper aims to establish a confidence interval for the ultimate ruin probability in an insurance surplus modeled by a Lévy process. By assuming a parametric form for the Lévy measures, the study estimates the parameters from surplus data and calculates the ruin probability using the delta method. However, since the asymptotic variance involves the derivative of the ruin probability with respect to the parameter—a term that is rarely available in closed form—the resulting confidence interval is difficult to derive, even when the ruin probability is accurately estimated. To address this, the paper provides a Cramér-type approximation for this derivative and derives an asymptotic confidence interval for the ruin probability.

The study of ionization losses—energy dissipation by fast charged particles moving through matter—has spanned over a century, with a comparable duration for its theoretical understanding. Roughly 75 years ago, Lev Landau published a seminal paper on this phenomenon that significantly accelerated research and remains one of the most cited works in the field. This note summarizes the history of the theoretical evolution, aiming to elucidate Landau's research methodology and the function that bears his name.

This work examines smooth Calabi-Yau 3-folds defined as complete intersections within minuscule Schubert varieties, investigating their mirror symmetry through the degeneration of these ambient varieties into Hibi toric varieties. We enumerate all such Calabi-Yau 3-folds up to deformation equivalence and identify a novel example of a smooth Calabi-Yau 3-fold with Picard number one: a complete intersection in a locally factorial Schubert variety ${\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$ of the Cayley plane ${\mathbb{OP}}^2$. Furthermore, we compute the topological invariants and BPS numbers for this specific Calabi-Yau 3-fold and propose that it possesses a non-trivial Fourier-Mukai partner.

We investigate magnetic excitations and spin-mediated superconductivity in iron-based superconductors using a low-energy model defined in the band basis that comprehensively accounts for the orbital nature of spin excitations. Our findings demonstrate that the orbital selectivity inherent in this low-energy framework significantly streamlines the analysis, enabling analytical solutions while preserving the essential characteristics of both spin excitations and gap functions derived from multiorbital models. Crucially, our study reveals that orbital matching between hole and electron pockets serves as the decisive factor for determining the momentum dependence and hierarchy of superconducting gaps, superseding the Fermi surface matching typical of standard nesting scenarios.

Good semigroups constitute a specific class of subsemigroups within $N^h$ that encompasses the value semigroups of rings linked to curve singularities and their blowups, thereby enabling a combinatorial analysis of these rings' properties. This paper provides a characterization of almost symmetric good subsemigroups of $N^h$, which generalizes established findings from numerical semigroup theory and one-dimensional ring theory, and subsequently utilizes these characterizations to derive novel results concerning almost Gorenstein one-dimensional analytically unramified rings.

Power efficiency represents a critical hurdle for untethered VR and AR hardware, as increasing computational demands driven by higher resolutions, refresh rates, and dynamic ranges directly conflict with battery longevity. For example, a fully charged Oculus Quest 2 offers only 2 to 3 hours of usage. While prior power-saving methods for smartphone displays exist, their direct application to AR/VR often compromises visual quality; smartphone "power-saving modes" typically dim the entire screen uniformly, resulting in a darkened experience unsuitable for immersive content. Our approach recognizes that VR display power reduction must account for the gaze-contingent nature of high field-of-view systems. We introduce a gaze-contingent system that minimizes power consumption without sacrificing luminance or visual fidelity during active viewing of immersive video. This is achieved by developing a gaze-contingent color discrimination model based on psychophysical research and a display power model derived from real-device measurements. Due to specific design choices in these models, the algorithm is formulated as a constrained optimization problem with a closed-form solution, allowing implementation as a real-time, image-space shader. Evaluation through psychophysical studies and extensive analysis of natural images demonstrates that the system can reduce display power by up to 24% with negligible impact on perceptual fidelity.

Managing spectrum sharing is a core challenge in wireless network administration. This paper addresses distributed spectrum collaboration in the absence of central control, specifically under conditions of unknown channels. Given that communication, coordination, and control costs escalate rapidly with device density and bandwidth expansion, there is a clear necessity for distributed collaboration techniques that eliminate explicit signaling. We integrate game-theoretic principles with deep Q-learning to offer a novel, asymptotically optimal solution for spectrum collaboration. Our proposed deterministic distributed deep reinforcement learning (D3RL) framework utilizes a deep Q-network (DQN) to select channels based on Q-values and current load. This approach restricts user options to a subset of channels with the highest Q-values, from which the least congested channel is chosen. Drawing on insights from game theory and combinatorial optimization, we demonstrate that this method achieves asymptotic optimality in large, overloaded networks. The system feeds back the selected channel and successful transmission outcomes to the DQN for continuous Q-value learning. Additionally, we analyzed performance to evaluate the behavior of D3RL in various scenarios.

Existing frameworks for the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of open chemical reaction networks are predicated on the assumption that species do not interact. We propose a comprehensive theory that incorporates inter-species interactions within a mean-field framework by utilizing activity coefficients. Thermodynamic consistency dictates that rate equations cannot adhere to standard mass-action kinetics; instead, they must incorporate concentration-dependent kinetic constants to reflect these interactions. While the theory recovers many characteristics of ideal formulations, it crucially identifies the thermodynamic potential and the driving forces for non-ideal systems moving away from equilibrium. This approach is broadly applicable to any mean-field interaction expression that results in lower-bounded free energies.

Analyzing data frequently requires comparing various subsets across numerous dimensions to identify anomalies and patterns. Although SQL can handle these comparisons, the resulting queries are often cumbersome and perform poorly on large, high-dimensional datasets. This paper introduces a novel logical operator, COMPARE, for relational databases that streamlines the enumeration and comparison of data subsets, thereby simplifying a wide range of comparative queries. We enhanced the database engine with optimization techniques that leverage the semantics of COMPARE to markedly boost query performance. These extensions were implemented within Microsoft SQL Server, a commercial DBMS. Our comprehensive evaluation using both synthetic and real-world data demonstrates that COMPARE delivers substantial speedups compared to current methods, including native physical plans, user-defined functions (UDFs), and middleware solutions that perform comparisons outside the database.

A set of multipartite orthogonal quantum states is defined as strongly nonlocal if it remains locally irreducible across every possible bipartition of its subsystems [Phys. Rev. Lett. 122, 040403 (2019)]. While this property has been demonstrated in systems with three, four, or five parts, the existence of such sets in $N$-partite systems for $N \geq 6$ was previously unknown. In this work, we prove that a strongly nonlocal set of orthogonal entangled states exists within $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes N}$ for all $N \geq 3$ and $d \geq 2$, thereby establishing the presence of strong quantum nonlocality in general $N$-partite systems for the first time. Specifically, for cases where $N=3$ or $4$ and $d \geq 3$, we introduce a strongly nonlocal set composed of genuinely entangled states that is smaller than any previously known strongly nonlocal orthogonal product set. Finally, we explore the relationship between strong quantum nonlocality and local hiding of information as a practical application.

The Turaev surface associated with a link diagram $D$ is a closed, oriented surface derived from a cobordism connecting the all-$A$ and all-$B$ Kauffman states of $D$. The Turaev genus of a link $L$ is defined as the minimal genus among the Turaev surfaces of all possible diagrams representing $L$. A link is alternating precisely when its Turaev genus equals zero, allowing Turaev genus one links to be regarded as nearly alternating. This paper investigates the Khovanov homology of such Turaev genus one links, focusing specifically on the first and last two polynomial gradings where the homology does not vanish. We demonstrate that a specific summand within the Khovanov homology of a Turaev genus one link is trivial. Consequently, this triviality enables the calculation of the Rasmussen $s$ invariant and establishes bounds on the smooth four-ball genus for specific Turaev genus one knots.

The Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) is a renowned optimization challenge within computer science and operations research, classified as NP-Hard. Even in its most basic form, TSP finds utility in fields like planning, logistics, and microchip manufacturing, and it can be adapted as a sub-problem for applications such as DNA sequencing. This paper examines the parallelization of the Brute Force method for solving the TSP across multiple paradigms. Additionally, it provides detailed timing analyses comparing serial and various parallel implementations of the problem.

Industrial process control systems demand reliable sensor-to-actuator communication within strict deadlines to ensure safe operation. WirelessHART is the leading standard for such industrial environments, leveraging features like TDMA-based communication, multiple channels, channel hopping, a centralized architecture, redundant routing, and avoidance of spatial reuse. However, because WirelessHART networks rely on a centralized manager to establish a fixed communication schedule at initialization—which then repeats every hyper-period—these systems suffer from predictable time slots. This predictability exposes them to timing attacks that can compromise system safety. To address this, we introduce SlotSwapper, a moving target defense mechanism that employs schedule randomization to vary time slots across hyper-periods. This approach maintains all real-time feasibility constraints while introducing uncertainty into the schedule every cycle. We validated the feasibility of the generated schedules using the Cooja simulator on random topologies comprising 100 simulated motes. Furthermore, we utilized schedule entropy to evaluate the algorithm's confidentiality regarding the randomness of the resulting time slots.

Local invariants for meromorphic quadratic differentials on compact Riemann surfaces consist of the orders of their zeros and poles, along with the residues at even-order poles. This paper demonstrates that, barring specific exceptions, any configuration of these local invariants can be realized by a quadratic differential on an appropriate Riemann surface. These exceptions are fully categorized and are confined to genera zero and one. Additionally, for nonconnected strata, it is proven that, aside from three cases in genus one, every set of invariants can be realized within each connected component of the stratum. These findings rely on the flat metric generated by the differentials. The study concludes with an application that establishes a bound on the number of disjoint cylinders found on a primitive quadratic differential.

Probing new physics relies heavily on measuring mixing-induced CP violation in Bs decays; however, to date, the Bs->J/\psi \phi channel has been the sole method employed. This study presents a measurement utilizing an LHCb dataset of 0.41/fb within the CP odd eigenstate J\psi f0(980), where f0(980) decays into \pi+ \pi-. By applying a time-dependent fit with the Bs lifetime and the width difference between heavy and light eigenstates constrained to values derived from Bs->J/\psi\phi, we determine the CP violating phase to be -0.44 +/- 0.44 +/- 0.02 rad, which aligns with Standard Model predictions.

The generalized $k$-connectivity, denoted as $\kappa_{k}(G)$, serves as a metric for assessing a graph $G$'s reliability in connecting any set of $k$ vertices; determining this value is known to be NP-complete for general graphs. Given a subset $S \subseteq V(G)$, let $\kappa_{G}(S)$ represent the maximum integer $r$ such that there exist $r$ edge-disjoint trees $T_{1}, T_{2}, \dots, T_{r}$ in $G$ where the intersection of the vertex sets of any distinct pair $T_i$ and $T_j$ is exactly $S$. For an integer $k$ satisfying $2 \leq k \leq n$, the generalized $k$-connectivity of $G$ is defined as $\kappa_{k}(G) = \min \{ \kappa_{G}(S) \mid S \subseteq V(G) \text{ and } |S| = k \}$. This paper investigates the generalized $3$-connectivity of certain recursively constructed general $m$-regular and $m$-connected graphs $G_{n}$, demonstrating that $\kappa_{3}(G_{n}) = m-1$. This result achieves the upper bound for $\kappa_{3}(G)$ previously established by Li et al. in *Discrete Mathematics* 310 (2010) for $G = G_{n}$. Furthermore, applying this main finding allows for the direct determination of the generalized $3$-connectivity for several well-known network topologies, including the alternating group graph $AG_{n}$, the $k$-ary $n$-cube $Q_{n}^{k}$, the split-star network $S_{n}^{2}$, and the bubble-sort-star graph $BS_{n}$.

Location-Based Recommendation Services (LBRS) have experienced a surge in popularity recently, offering users suggestions tailored to their geographic position and historical preferences. However, utilizing these services entails significant privacy risks, as users must disclose sensitive data—such as dining habits, travel history, and accommodation choices—to third-party servers, potentially compromising their personal security. In response to this growing concern for privacy, new solutions leveraging Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) have emerged to mitigate these risks. While effective, FHE-based systems incur substantial computational costs that hinder their practical commercial deployment. To address this, we introduce SHELBRS, a lightweight LBRS framework built upon Switchable Homomorphic Encryption (SHE). This approach harnesses both additive and multiplicative homomorphic properties while significantly reducing processing time compared to FHE, thereby benefiting both users and service providers. Our evaluation demonstrates that SHELBRS achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods without sacrificing security.

Since their discovery, muons have perplexed physicists, initially being mistaken for the mesons Yukawa predicted to mediate the strong force. Recent findings regarding the muon g-2 anomaly at Fermilab have once again highlighted the importance of this particle, urging new measurements. This work reports the first measurement of the $2S_{1/2},F$=$0 \rightarrow 2P_{1/2},F$=$1$ transition in Muonium, a hydrogen-like system composed of an electron and a positive muon. The observed value of 580.6 $\pm$6.8 MHz aligns with theoretical predictions. Consequently, a Lamb shift of 1045.5 $\pm$6.8 MHz is derived, consistent with prior experimental results. Additionally, we determine the $2S$ hyperfine splitting in Muonium for the first time as 559.6$\pm$7.2 MHz. Because this specific transition is isolated from other hyperfine levels, it offers the potential to refine the determination of the Muonium Lamb shift to a precision where bound-state QED recoil corrections—unreachable in hydrogen—can be tested. This measurement is also sensitive to new physics within the muonic sector, such as new bosons that could explain the g-2 anomaly or violations of Lorentz and CPT symmetry. Furthermore, we report the first observation of Muonium in the $n=3$ excited state, enabling the possibility of new precise microwave measurements similar to those conducted in hydrogen.

We introduce a catalog of radio sources within the M 17 region, derived from deep 10 GHz X-band observations conducted by the Jansky Very Large Array in its A configuration. Our survey identified 194 radio sources, comprising 12 extended and 182 compact objects. At least 40% of these sources exhibit suspected gyrosynchrotron emission linked to stellar coronal activity. When comparing our sources' radio luminosities to available X-ray counterparts, we observe that they are X-ray underluminous relative to the G\"udel-Benz relation; however, a correlation with a comparable slope emerges when selecting only sources with evident non-thermal characteristics from samples of the Orion Nebula Cluster (ONC) and M 17. Comparing M 17 with the ONC and NGC 6334D-F reveals a similar luminosity function for the three regions, particularly among the more luminous sources. Nevertheless, at any given luminosity, M 17 contains three times as many radio sources as the other regions, and its spatial distribution differs from that of Orion. Additionally, our map detects a 40$"$ arc-shaped structure, previously identified as an ionizing front, with the cometary Hyper Compact source UC1 at its center. Archival 1 mm ALMA data shows compact emission coinciding with the radio peak, potentially indicating a protostellar disk around the massive star driving UC1.

Origin-Destination (OD) matrices capture directional flow data between various OD regions. The complex spatiotemporal dependencies within these matrices render the OD matrix forecasting (ODMF) task both challenging and non-trivial. However, existing methods are typically tailored for short-term time series forecasting in specific contexts, failing to satisfy the diverse requirements regarding scenario variations and forecasting durations found in practical applications. To overcome these limitations, we introduce ODformer, a Transformer-inspired model featuring two key innovations: (i) a novel OD Attention mechanism that identifies unique spatial dependencies among OD pairs sharing the same origin or destination; when integrated with a 2D-GCN to model spatial relationships between OD regions, this significantly enhances the model's adaptability across different application scenarios. (ii) A PeriodSparse Self-attention module that enables effective long-sequence forecasting of OD matrix series while accommodating periodic variations across distinct scenarios. Extensive experiments across three domains—transportation traffic, IP backbone network traffic, and crowd flow—demonstrate that our method surpasses current state-of-the-art approaches.

As cloud storage adoption increases, eliminating duplicate data across users has become essential for service providers to cut costs. Recently, data resemblance detection has emerged as a novel technology to identify redundancy among similar items by extracting features from chunk contents and treating highly similar chunks as redundancy candidates. However, prevalent methods like "N-transform" and "Finesse" rely solely on chunk data for feature extraction, meaning even minor modifications to a chunk can severely degrade detection accuracy. To address this limitation, this paper proposes CARD, a novel chunk-context aware resemblance detection algorithm. CARD employs a BP-Neural network-based model that integrates both the internal structure of data chunks and their surrounding context for feature extraction, significantly reducing the impact of small data variations. We implemented a CARD prototype and conducted extensive experiments using real-world datasets. The results demonstrate that CARD detects up to 75.03% more redundant data and accelerates resemblance detection operations by 5.6 to 17.8 times compared to current state-of-the-art approaches.

Modern society increasingly depends on classifiers for critical decisions, creating a demand for ethical safeguards like fairness. This concept is generally defined by ensuring specific statistical metrics remain roughly consistent across protected population groups. This paper reviews existing fairness strategies to inspire new algorithmic approaches that integrate fairness into genetic programming for classification tasks. We introduce two key proposals: first, embedding a fairness objective within multi-objective optimization; second, adapting lexicase selection to dynamically define cases based on intersections of protected groups. We explain why lexicase selection effectively pressures models to perform well across the potentially infinite subgroups relevant to fairness. Using a recent genetic programming framework, we constructed models on four datasets requiring fairness constraints and empirically compared their performance against prior methods utilizing game-theoretic solutions. Evaluation focused on the ability to generate Pareto-optimal trade-offs between subgroup fairness and accuracy. The results indicate that genetic programming methods, and random search specifically, are particularly well-suited for this objective.

This research investigates the social welfare loss resulting from corrupt auctioneers in both single-item and multi-unit auction formats. The model posits that an auctioneer may collude with winning bidders, allowing them to submit reduced bids in return for a fraction $\gamma$ of the surplus, which varies depending on the bidder. We examine various corruption mechanisms, starting with the simplest scenario where all winners bid down to the highest losing bid. We demonstrate that this scenario is equivalent to a $\gamma$-hybrid auction, where payments represent a convex combination of first-price and second-price rules. More broadly, we analyze corruption schemes akin to $\gamma$-approximate first-price auctions ($\gamma$-FPA), in which payments recover at least a $\gamma$-portion of the standard first-price payments. The primary objective is to precisely determine the robust price of anarchy (POA) for these auction types. Without bid restrictions, we establish a tight bound on the robust POA of $\gamma$-FPA that holds across the full spectrum of $\gamma$ for both single-item and multi-unit settings. Conversely, under the assumption of no overbidding, a more nuanced landscape of the price of anarchy emerges, contingent upon the specific auction format and equilibrium concept. Although more complex, we derive (almost) tight bounds for both auction types and multiple equilibrium notions, leaving only minor gaps unresolved regarding the coarse-correlated price of anarchy.

We introduce an enhanced random spreading technique for unsourced multiple access utilizing polar codes. In this scheme, every user encodes its message via a polar code, which is subsequently spread using a random sequence. The method partitions active users into distinct groups, assigning specific power levels to each group to adhere to the average power constraint. We formulate and resolve an optimization problem to identify the optimal number of groups, the user count per group, and the corresponding power levels. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that this approach surpasses current methods, particularly in scenarios with a high number of active users.

A wide range of integrable stochastic particle systems in one dimension, including the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP) and its deformations (excluding ASEP), retain integrability even when assigned individual jump rate parameters $
u_i$ to each particle $x_i$. Due to this integrability, the distribution of any particle $x_n(t)$, starting from a step configuration, depends symmetrically on the parameters $
u_j$ for $j \le n$. Consequently, swapping parameters $
u_n$ and $
u_{n+1}$ influences only the distribution of $x_n(t)$. For the $q$-Hahn TASEP and its degenerates (such as $q$-TASEP and the directed beta polymer), this parameter transposition is realized as an explicit Markov swap operator acting on particle $x_n(t)$. In the case of the beta polymer, the swap operator corresponds to a straightforward modification of the underlying lattice. The analysis relies primarily on Markov duality and contour integral formulas for joint moments. These tools yield a continuous-time Markov process $\mathsf{Q}^{(\mathsf{t})}$ that preserves the time-$\mathsf{t}$ distribution of $q$-TASEP (with step initial conditions, where $\mathsf{t} \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is fixed); its dual is a specific transient variant of the stochastic $q$-Boson system. By equating asymptotic survival probabilities of this transient process with $q$-moments of $q$-TASEP, we demonstrate the convergence of $\mathsf{Q}^{(\mathsf{t})}$ to its stationary distribution regardless of initial data. When $q=0$, these findings align with recent results on standard TASEP (from [arXiv:1907.09155]), which were derived using a distinct approach based on two-dimensional interlacing particle Gibbs ensembles.

This note examines the extended hull of a weak model set alongside its natural shift action, equipped with the Mirsky measure—a natural metric for pattern frequencies. It is established that the extended hull serves as a measure-theoretic factor of a group rotation known as the underlying torus. In our previous work, "Periods and factors of weak model sets," we demonstrated that for weak model sets with compact windows, the extended hull is isomorphic to a factor group of the torus, obtained by factoring out specific periods of the window. In this paper, we extend these findings to arbitrary measurable and relatively compact windows. Our proof primarily depends on Moody's research regarding uniform distribution in model sets. Furthermore, we explore the implications for the diffraction properties of these weak model sets and introduce a new class of examples that are generic with respect to the Mirsky measure.

Molecular dynamics simulations utilizing a chain model demonstrate that multilayer assemblies of identical single-walled carbon nanotubes (with a diameter D > 2.5 nm) on a flat substrate constitute a multistable system. This system features numerous stationary states, each defined by the fraction of collapsed nanotubes; consequently, the package thickness decreases monotonically as the proportion of collapsed tubes increases. Specifically, for nanotubes with a chirality index of (60,0), the thickness of an 11-layer package can range from 12 to 36 nm depending on the degree of collapse. All these stationary states remain stable against thermal fluctuations at 300 K. Furthermore, the transverse compression of the package is non-elastic; instead of recovering, it merely transitions the system from one stationary state to another with reduced thickness due to further nanotube collapse.

This study introduces cyclic and minimal derivative descendants (DDs) of an extended cyclic code, derived respectively from the Mattson-Solomon polynomials. Initially, it establishes that cyclic DDs correspond to the same extended cyclic code, enabling soft-decision decoding via these cyclic DDs. Subsequently, it demonstrates that minimal DDs represent equivalent codes, which facilitates soft-decision decoding through minimal DDs combined with permutations. Simulation outcomes indicate that the proposed derivative decoding approach achieves performance nearly matching maximum likelihood decoding for specific extended cyclic codes, such as certain extended BCH codes.

This study details the custom development, optimization, and performance assessment of convolutional neural networks deployed on field programmable gate arrays to accelerate deep neural network inference for large, two-dimensional image inputs. The specific application focuses on data selection for high-resolution particle imaging detectors, particularly liquid argon time projection chambers (LArTPCs) like those planned for the future Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment. This focus is driven by the superior classification performance of deep neural networks on simulated raw DUNE LArTPC data, alongside the critical requirement for power-efficient data processing under remote, long-term, and limited-access operating conditions.

We re-examine the conventional construction of the celestial stress tensor as a shadow of the subleading conformally soft graviton. While the original formulation encounters an obstacle in reproducing the expected TT OPE within the double soft limit, we introduce a modified definition that resolves this issue. Furthermore, we generalize this basis transformation beyond the conformally soft and single helicity sectors. Throughout this process, we explore the relationship between the (non)-commutativity of double soft limits and the decoupling of primary descendants, as well as how our selected celestial basis dictates which symmetries become explicit in the OPE beyond the MHV sector.

This letter examines the secrecy rate of a millimeter-wave (mmWave) system assisted by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) under hardware constraints. Unlike most existing studies on RIS-aided systems, our work specifically addresses scenarios involving low-resolution digital-to-analog converters (LDACs). We formulate a secrecy rate maximization problem subject to these hardware limitations and aim to optimize the RIS phase shifts and transmit beamforming. However, the problem's nonconvex nature makes it intractable. To address this, we propose an alternating optimization (AO)-based algorithm. Specifically, we employ the successive convex approximation (SCA) method to derive the transmit beamforming and the element-wise block coordinate descent (BCD) method to determine the RIS phase shifts. Numerical results indicate that the RIS can effectively mitigate hardware losses, and the proposed low-complexity AO-based algorithm outperforms existing baselines.

Building upon the classical contraction mapping principle, we develop a broad and adaptable variational framework that proves effective for numerous existence problems in Differential Equations. We demonstrate its versatility through specific examples, covering initial-value and Cauchy problems for ODEs, non-linear monotone PDEs, both linear and non-linear hyperbolic equations, and steady Navier-Stokes systems.

Camera and LiDAR sensors offer complementary appearance and geometric data essential for 3D object detection in autonomous driving. However, existing end-to-end fusion techniques are difficult to train and often lag behind state-of-the-art LiDAR-only models. Sequential fusion approaches face challenges such as limited pixel-point correspondences caused by point cloud sparsity, or their performance is constrained by the capabilities of a single modality. We introduce Dense Voxel Fusion (DVF), a sequential fusion strategy that creates multi-scale dense voxel feature representations, thereby enhancing expressiveness in areas with sparse point density. To improve multi-modal learning, we train directly using projected ground truth 3D bounding box labels, bypassing noisy, detector-specific 2D predictions. Both DVF and our multi-modal training framework are compatible with any voxel-based LiDAR backbone. On the KITTI 3D car detection benchmark, DVF ranks 3rd among published fusion methods without adding trainable parameters or requiring stereo images or dense depth labels. Furthermore, DVF substantially boosts 3D vehicle detection performance for voxel-based methods on the Waymo Open Dataset.

We present a record-breaking thermoelectric figure of merit ($ZT$) reaching up to 6 at 1100 K in $n$-doped lanthanum oxysulphate (LaSO). Thermoelectric coefficients were calculated using ab initio band structures within the Bloch-Boltzmann framework, utilizing a relaxation time approximation that accounts for variations in energy, chemical potential, and temperature. The lattice thermal conductivity was estimated through a model incorporating ab initio phonon spectra and Gr\"uneisen parameters. The exceptionally high $ZT$ primarily stems from a substantial power factor, which is linked to a large band complexity factor. Furthermore, we propose a viable $n$-type dopant for this material based on ab initio computational results.

This paper initiates research into local model reconstruction attacks within federated learning, where an honest-but-curious adversary intercepts communications between a specific client and the server to reconstruct the victim's personalized local model. This type of attack is more potent than traditional ones because the local model relies solely on the client's data, exposing greater private information than the server's global model. Consequently, it enables other classical attacks to be executed more effectively. Furthermore, we introduce a new model-based attribute inference attack that utilizes local model reconstruction and establish an analytical lower bound for it. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate the efficacy of our local reconstruction attack across both classification and regression tasks. Additionally, we evaluate our attribute inference attack against current state-of-the-art methods in federated learning, showing superior reconstruction accuracy, particularly in scenarios with heterogeneous client data. Our findings offer a novel perspective for developing powerful, explainable attacks to better quantify privacy risks in federated learning.

Clarifying why specific items are recommended is essential, as it aids users in making superior decisions, enhances their satisfaction, and fosters trust in recommender systems (RS). However, current explainable RS approaches typically treat explanations as auxiliary outputs of the recommendation model, leading to two key issues: (1) the resulting explanations are hard to evaluate because they are often model-specific, and (2) the extent to which these explanations influence recommendation performance remains underexplored. This paper reframes explanation generation as a ranking task learned from data, analogous to standard item ranking. This approach enables the use of conventional ranking metrics (such as NDCG) for evaluating explanations. Moreover, the study extends traditional item ranking to a joint item-explanation ranking framework to investigate whether intentionally selecting explanations can achieve specific learning objectives, such as boosting recommendation accuracy. A significant challenge arises from the increased data sparsity in user-item-explanation interactions compared to traditional user-item data, as not every pair is linked to all possible explanations. To address this, the paper proposes performing two sets of matrix factorization by decomposing the ternary relationship into two groups of binary relationships. Experiments across three large datasets confirm the proposed method's effectiveness in both explanation ranking and item recommendation.

Although retracted research discussed on social media can propagate misinformation, our understanding of how both academic and non-academic users reference these articles remains limited, a gap that is particularly significant given Twitter's central role in science communication. This study examines the differences in Twitter engagement metrics and content surrounding over 3,800 retracted English-language articles compared to similar non-retracted ones, analyzing data both before and after retraction. We categorize these findings using five user types identified by a supervised learning classifier: the general public, scientists, bots, practitioners, and science communicators. Our results indicate that retracted articles attract higher overall engagement than non-retracted ones, a trend driven primarily by the public and bot users, with most interactions occurring prior to the retraction. These findings underscore the involvement of non-scientists in discussions about retracted articles and propose that Twitter should implement a feature to display retraction notices.

WebAssembly (wasm) has recently established itself as a secure, efficient, fast, and portable binary format for the web. However, its ability to interact freely with JavaScript libraries creates a risk of undesirable behavior, making detection mechanisms essential. One such approach is taint tracking, which monitors information flow by assigning taint labels to data. This paper introduces TaintAssembly, a taint tracking engine designed for interpreted WebAssembly, developed by modifying the V8 JavaScript engine. We implemented core taint tracking capabilities, including tainting linear memory and a probabilistic taint variant. We evaluated the TaintAssembly engine by integrating it into a Chromium build and testing it against custom scripts and various real-world WebAssembly applications. Our results indicate that the modifications to V8 do not introduce significant overhead compared to standard interpreted WebAssembly, rendering TaintAssembly well-suited for development and debugging purposes.

Recent advancements have enabled supervised fine-tuning of pretrained GPT-2 models to create end-to-end task-oriented dialog (TOD) systems; however, the online reinforcement learning of a GPT-2-based dialog system (DS) paired with an end-to-end user simulator (US) remains unexplored. Furthermore, current GPT-2-based TOD systems typically rely on the entire dialog history as input, leading to inefficiencies in memory usage and computation. This paper introduces Simplified Generative Architectures (SGA) for both the DS and US, utilizing GPT-2 with truncated history. We subsequently develop SGA-JRUD, a jointly reinforced US and DS. Our DS, trained solely through supervision with the proposed SGA, achieves state-of-the-art results on MultiWOZ2.1 while offering superior compute efficiency during both training and generation. Additional extensive experiments on MultiWOZ2.1 demonstrate that SGA-JRUD outperforms existing methods in both offline and online evaluations.

Proton therapy is an evolving modality defined by a Bragg peak—a sharp dose maximum at the end of the trajectory followed by a rapid decline—which allows for highly conformal tumor targeting while sparing healthy tissues and organs at risk. Although modern treatment planning systems utilizing spot scanning can now suggest multi-field optimizations, these typically optimize only field fluences, leaving the selection of beam geometries (ballistics) to the discretion of the oncologist and medical physicist.

This study introduces a novel optimization framework grounded in a genetic algorithm, designed to explore diverse irradiation strategies and assess the capabilities of current or future systems. We propose a method that simultaneously optimizes target points and beam incidence angles continuously, allowing for a variable number of beams without *a priori* technological constraints; specifically, beam energies, incidence directions, and target locations are treated as free parameters.

The algorithm employs a modified set of classical genetic operators—mutation, crossover, and selection. By utilizing real-coded parameters with random perturbations, we achieve continuous variation in potential solutions. Additionally, we incorporate a perturbation mechanism within the crossover exchange points to enable variations in the number of beams, regulated by a minimum beam fluence threshold.

This paper provides a comprehensive description of the algorithm and its performance on an elementary test case, followed by an evaluation using a clinically realistic scenario.

This study offers new perspectives on the origin of the high-field Q-slope in superconducting radio-frequency cavities. To investigate how radio-frequency performance varies with material removal, we employed hydrofluoric acid rinses on two bulk niobium cavities fabricated using low-temperature nitrogen infusion. The findings indicate that nitrogen infusion influences only the initial few tens of nanometers beneath the native oxide layer. Consequently, the characteristic high-field Q-slope behavior observed in electropolished cavities is fully restored after approximately twelve hydrofluoric acid rinses. Furthermore, the resurgence of the high-field Q-slope relative to material removal was modeled using London's local description of screening currents in superconductors; this approach yielded an excellent fit to the experimental data and suggests that interstitial impurity layers, with diffusion lengths on the order of tens of nanometers, can mitigate the high-field Q-slope.

The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is recognized for its versatility and effectiveness in addressing combinatorial optimization tasks on near-term quantum hardware. However, the outcomes of QAOA are highly sensitive to their initial variational parameters. Consequently, parameter selection has become a focal point of research, as poor initialization can significantly degrade result quality, particularly as circuit depth increases. This study first examines optimal parameter patterns across two dimensions: the angle index and circuit depth. It then explores the symmetries and periodicity of the expectation values used to define search space boundaries. Leveraging these patterns and constraints, we introduce a strategy that forecasts new initial parameters by calculating the difference between previously optimal ones. Distinct from most existing approaches, this method does not necessitate multiple trials for success; it requires only a single prediction when advancing to the next depth. We evaluate this approach against our prior strategy and the layerwise method by solving the Max-cut problem, assessing performance based on approximation ratio and optimization cost. Furthermore, we address the issue of non-optimality in previous parameters—a critical yet underexplored aspect in current literature that is essential for understanding the behavior of variational quantum algorithms.

Dark matter (DM) detectors utilizing Spherical Proportional Counters (SPCs) have already achieved single-electron detection thresholds and are anticipated to maintain low background rates. This study examines the sensitivity of SPC detectors to DM-electron scattering within the framework of DarkSphere, a proposed 300 cm diameter fully-electroformed SPC. Given the ability of SPCs to operate with various gases, we analyzed the sensitivity across five specific targets: helium, neon, xenon, methane, and isobutane. By applying quantum chemistry tools to model atomic and molecular systems, we calculated the expected event rates induced by DM interactions. Our findings indicate that DarkSphere could enhance current exclusion limits on DM masses exceeding 4 MeV by up to five orders of magnitude. While neon emerges as the optimal all-around gas target, incorporating gas mixtures where methane and isobutane comprise 10% of the composition can further boost sensitivity, particularly when paired with helium. This research underscores the currently underutilized potential of SPCs for detecting DM-electron scattering within the MeV-to-GeV DM mass spectrum.

The introduction of modern spectrum categories, such as those by Elmendorf et al., which feature strictly symmetric monoidal smash products, enables the definition of symmetric monoids. This development offers a novel approach to investigating highly coherent commutative ring spectra. These spectra possess module categories that generalize classical spectrum categories, which correspond to modules over the sphere spectrum.
